Tip number five is to position your take or stance to drive significant emotion. The more people feel something when they watch your video, the more they're going to feel compelled to want to comment. I did a side-by-side comparison to compare and contrast their mechanics in the acceleration and high speed phases of the sprint. Coming out of the blocks, both Erling and Kylian display a similar sprinter’s starting stance with the body leaning forwards, driving the hip upwards and extending the other leg to explode forward, and using a prominent contralateral arm swing. One key difference here is that Erling tends rounds his upper back and dip his head downwards whereas Kylian’s neck and head is more aligned with the rest of his body. As both players get to higher speed, the players exhibit similar upright torsos and long strides with less pronounced hip flexion. Haaland’s arm swing tends to be a little more pronounced and across his body but the key, key difference between the two is the back leg - Mbappe really gets that back leg into extension at the hip and knee whereas Haaland doesn’t. This may be a key mechanical reason for the difference in speed. Lastly - both players exhibit a similar oval shape with their feet and the heels turning up high along with fast ground contact times (generally this ranges from .07 to .1 seconds for elite sprinters) For the most part, both exhibit similar sprinting mechanics with Haaland’s a bit more outside the norm, potentially due to his size.   1. @malmiteria [3 likes]: 5:00 no offense but creating a function called saveFormatted that has the only responsibility to call ... saveFormatted... huh?!

such a junior mistake. You already have a function that does the job, call it, that's it. No need for an extra function that exclusively calls the function you wanted in the first place.

Same for splitting formatAndSaveName
It only makes sense because you completely ignored the "call" side of those function, and unquestioningly consider any side effects to be bad.
Everywhere you called that function, you now have to call both format and save, which both makes it a huge source of bugs, by making it easy to forget one of them, and completely misses the point of API abstractions.

Not only that, but the fact is, you'd have to call them both everytime or so, making the idea of separation of concerns really not apply here.
Formatting and saving are really really really related concerns, not separate, when your task is to format and save.

In any case, we've seen large language models in particular grow 2,000 times in size over the last five years. And of course, their environmental costs are rising as well. The most recent work I led, found that switching out a smaller, more efficient model for a larger language model emits 14 times more carbon for the same task. Like telling that knock-knock joke. And as we're putting in these models into cell phones and search engines and smart fridges and speakers, the environmental costs are really piling up quickly. So instead of focusing on some future existential risks, let's talk about current tangible impacts and tools we can create to measure and mitigate these impacts. I helped create CodeCarbon, a tool that runs in parallel to AI training code that estimates the amount of energy it consumes and the amount of carbon it emits.   18. @f3rn4n2x3str3ll4: Since you were advocating for introspection, consider this:
Every post in social media can be seen as a response to the question “how to be happy?”.
Example: Your friend posts a travel picture. They just say something about what they experienced, in the caption, like: “I spent the whole night up and didn’t feel tired!”. But they were implicitly saying: “I was feeling like my daily routine was narrowing my view of the world and life, so I aimed to expand it with travel. When I traveled, I did all these things and this is how well it served my intended purpose”. Since no one is requesting your friend to be explicit about those 3 components (the problem/goal, the method they used to achieve that goal, and how well it worked) your friend doesn’t explain them explicitly. But everyone should be explicit about them. 
Why?
Because it would help someone else. If someone else had the same goal as you, they could see what worked for you, and if you evaluate that method very positively, they would compare your rating to the rating they give to the method they were trying so far or considering, and may try your method instead. Yes, maybe a “10/10” rating is subjective for everyone, but it would still give some sense of ”objective” measure of effectiveness.
So, everyone can say the components  explicitly, or social media could request you to fill in those 3 components for every post you make, so it’s easier for the software to find all posts that are describing how to reach a given goal, all the methods tried to achieve that goal, and all the ratings.
Now, social media could be designed with those components as the basis of the design. You could just login and search for a goal or create one if yours doesn’t exist, see the methods that exist to achieve that goal, which ones have been tried by people, and how people have evaluated every attempt. They could add nuance or extra details to their numeric review with an extra text field.
I was thinking of what would be the fastest way to implement such a social media nowadays, and my current conclusion is that it can be in a Discord server: each channel can be a goal, each post in a channel is a method, and each reply to a post is a review of someone’s attempt to use that method to reach that goal. Everyone can quickly find methods to try and they can leave their reviews after giving an honest attempt. If the nature of some attempt really requires a person to update their evaluation or append to it, it would be best that they update the same review instead of creating new ones that are harder to link together. What they can do is start a review, grab a link to the reply they just made, and save it as a bookmark so they can come back to it later. I created such a Discord server but haven’t shared it with anyone yet. No reason for it, just doing something else.
More broadly, this system leverages the core of what looking for truth is: if you really want to reach your goal, you want to know what the TRUE method to reach your goal is. Why? Because reality works a certain way. I’m not implying it is a limited way. It just works in some way. You want to operate in the way reality actually works. 
So, when using this system, users are not distracted by prejudices they may have regarding where a method came from. Even though someone may suggest a method that was originally from a tradition, philosophy, body of work, experiment, culture, religion, etc., the method is simply presented as the essence what it is: a standalone method to reach the goal you chose to reach, instead of one part of many others that you must ascribe by to reach the goal someone else tells you you should reach. That is, the prejudice may come from the fact that someone is offering you more than what you need, e.g. “join my culture, do all these things, and then you will get this goal” so you wonder "do I need all that?", and from the fact that someone is offering you to reach a goal that you haven’t chosen yourself that you want to reach, e.g. if someone offers you a method to feel the whole universe as part of you, you may not be sure if you want it when all you want right now is not to feel angry with someone.

- Algorithmic Bias and Fairness: Crash Course AI #18: Kind: captions Language: en Hi, I’m Jabril and welcome back to CrashCourse AI. Algorithms are just math and code, but algorithms are created by people and use our data, so biases that exist in the real world are mimicked or even exaggerated by AI systems. This idea is called algorithmic bias. Bias isn’t inherently a terrible thing. Our brains try to take shortcuts by finding patterns in data. So if you’ve only seen small, tiny dogs, you might see a Great Dane and be like “Whoa that dog is unnatural” This doesn’t become a problem unless we don’t acknowledge exceptions to patterns or unless we start treating certain groups of people unfairly. As a society, we have laws to prevent discrimination based on certain “protected classes” (like gender, race, or age) for things like employment or housing. So it’s important to be aware of the difference between bias, which we all have, and discrimination, which we can prevent. And knowing about algorithmic bias can help us steer clear of a future where AI are used in harmful, discriminatory ways. INTRO There are at least 5 types of algorithmic bias we should pay attention to. First, training data can reflect hidden biases in society. For example, if an AI was trained on recent news articles or books, the word “nurse” is more likely to refer to a “woman,” while the word “programmer” is more likely to refer to a “man.” And you can see this happening with a Google image search: “nurse” shows mostly women, while “programmer” mostly shows mostly men. We can see how hidden biases in the data gets embedded in search engine AI. Of course, we know there are male nurses and female programmers and non-binary people doing both of these jobs! For example, an image search for “programmer 1960” shows a LOT more women. But AI algorithms aren’t very good at recognizing cultural biases that might change over time, and they could even be spreading hidden biases to more human brains. t’s also tempting to think that if we just don’t collect or use training data that categorizes protected classes like race or gender, then our algorithms can’t possibly discriminate. But, protected classes may emerge as correlated features, which are features that aren’t explicitly in data but may be unintentionally correlated to a specific prediction. For example, because many places in the US are still extremely segregated, zip code can be strongly correlated to race. A record of purchases can be strongly correlated to gender. And a controversial 2017 paper showed that sexual orientation is strongly correlated with characteristics of a social media profile photo. Second, the training data may not have enough examples of each class, which can affect the accuracy of predictions. For example, many facial recognition AI algorithms are trained on data that includes way more examples of white peoples’ faces than other races. One story that made the news a few years ago is a passport photo checker with an AI system to warn if the person in the photo had blinked. But the system had a lot of trouble with photos of people of Asian descent. Being asked to take a photo again and again would be really frustrating if you’re just trying to renew your passport, which is already sort of a pain! Or, let’s say, you got a cool gig programming a drone for IBM… but it has trouble recognizing your face because your skin’s too dark… for example. Third, it’s hard to quantify certain features in training data. There are lots of things that are tough to describe with numbers. Like can you really rate a sibling relationship with a number? It’s complicated! You love them, but you hate how messy they are, but you like cooking together, but you hate how your parents compare you... It’s so hard to quantify all that! In many cases, we try to build AI to evaluate complicated qualities of data, but sometimes we have to settle for easily measurable shortcuts. One recent example is trying to use AI to grade writing on standardized tests like SATs and GREs with the goal to save human graders time. Good writing involves complex elements like clarity, structure, and creativity, but most of these qualities are hard to measure. So, instead, these AI focused on easier-to-measure elements like sentence length, vocabulary, and grammar, which don’t fully represent good writing… and made these AIs easier to fool. Some students from MIT built a natural language program to create essays that made NO sense, but were rated highly by these grading algorithms. These AIs could also potentially be fooled by memorizing portions of “template” essays to influence the score, rather than actually writing a response to the prompt, all because of the training data that was used for these scoring AI. Fourth, the algorithm could influence the data that it gets, creating a positive feedback loop. A positive feedback loop basically means “amplifying what happened in the past”… whether or not this amplification is good. An example is PredPol’s drug crime prediction algorithm, which has been in use since 2012 in many large cities including LA and Chicago. PredPol was trained on data that was heavily biased by past housing segregation and past cases of police bias. So, it would more frequently send police to certain neighborhoods where a lot of racial minority folks lived. Arrests in those neighborhoods increased, that arrest data was fed back into the algorithm, and the AI would predict more future drug arrests in those neighborhoods and send the police there again. Even though there might be crime in neighborhoods where police weren’t being sent by this AI, because there weren't any arrests in those neighborhoods, data about them wasn’t fed back into the algorithm. While algorithms like PredPol are still in use, to try and manage these feedback effects, there is currently more effort to monitor and adjust how they process data. So basically, this would be like a new principal who was hired to improve the average grades of a school, but he doesn’t really care about the students who already have good grades. He creates a watchlist of students who have really bad grades and checks up on them every week, and he ignores the students who keep up with good grades. If any of the students on his watchlist don’t do their homework that week, they get punished. But all of the students NOT on his watchlist can slack on their homework, and get away with it based on “what happened in the past.” This is essentially what’s happening with PredPol, and you can be the judge if you believe it’s fair or not. Finally, a group of people may mess with training data on purpose. For example, in 2014, Microsoft released a chatbot named Xiaoice in China. People could chat with Xiaoice so it would learn how to speak naturally on a variety of topics from these conversations. It worked great, and Xiaoice had over 40 million conversations with no incidents. In 2016, Microsoft tried the same thing in the U.S. by releasing the Twitterbot Tay. Tay trained on direct conversation threads on Twitter, and by playing games with users where they could get it to repeat what they were saying. In 12 hours after its release, after a “coordinated attack by a subset of people” who biased its data set, Tay started posting violent, sexist, anti-semitic, and racist Tweets. This kind of manipulation is usually framed as “joking” or “trolling,” but the fact that AI can be manipulated means we should take algorithmic predictions with a grain of salt. This is why I don’t leave John-Green-Bot alone online… The common theme of algorithmic bias is that AI systems are trying to make good predictions, but they make mistakes. Some of these mistakes may be harmless or mildly inconvenient, but others may have significant consequences. To understand the key limitations of AI in our current society, let’s go to the Thought Bubble. Let’s say there’s an AI system called HireMe! that gives hiring recommendations to companies. HireMe is being used by Robots Weekly, a magazine where John-Green-bot applied for an editorial job. Just by chance, the last two people named “John” got fired from Robots Weekly and another three “Johns” didn’t make it through the hiring process. So, when John-Green-Bot applies for the job, HireMe! predicts that he’s only 24% likely to be employed by the company in 3 years. Seeing this prediction, the hiring manager at Robots Weekly rejects John-Green-bot, and this data gets added to the HireMe! AI system. John-Green-Bot is just another “John” that got rejected, even though he may have been the perfect robot for the job! Now, future “Johns” have an even lower chance to be hired. It’s a positive feedback loop, with some pretty negative consequences for John-Green-Bot. Of course, being named “John” isn’t a protected class, but this could apply to other groups of people. Plus, even though algorithms like HireMe! Are great at establishing a link between two kinds of data, they can’t always clarify why they’re making predictions. For example, HireMe! may find that higher age is associated with lower knowledge of digital technologies, so the AI suggests hiring younger applicants. Not only is this illegally discriminating against the protected class of “age,” but the implied link also might not be true. John-Green-bot may be almost 40, but he runs a robot blog and is active in online communities like Nerdfighteria! So it’s up to humans interacting with AI systems like HireMe! to pay attention to recommendations and make sure they’re fair, or adjust the algorithms if not. Thanks, Thought Bubble! Monitoring AI for bias and discrimination sounds like a huge responsibility, so how can we do it? The first step is just understanding that algorithms will be biased. It’s important to be critical about AI recommendations, instead of just accepting that “the computer said so.” This is why transparency in algorithms is so important, which is the ability to examine inputs and outputs to understand why an algorithm is giving certain recommendations. But that's easier said than done when it comes to certain algorithms, like deep learning methods. Hidden layers can be tricky to interpret. Second, if we want to have less biased algorithms, we may need more training data on protected classes like race, gender, or age. Looking at an algorithm’s recommendations for protected classes may be a good way to check it for discrimination. This is kind of a double-edged sword, though. People who are part of protected classes may (understandably) be worried about handing over personal information. It may feel like a violation of privacy, or they might worry that algorithms will be misused to target rather than protect them. Even if you aren’t actively working on AI systems, knowing about these algorithms and staying informed about artificial intelligence are really important as we shape the future of this field. Anyone, including you, can advocate for more careful, critical interpretation of algorithmic outputs to help protect human rights. Some people are even advocating that algorithms should be clinically tested and scrutinized in the same way that medicines are. According to these opinions, we should know if there are “side effects” before integrating AI in our daily lives. There’s nothing like that in the works yet. But it took over 2400 years for the Hippocratic Oath to transform into current medical ethics guidelines. So it may take some time for us to come up with the right set of practices. Next time, we have a lab and I’ll demonstrate how there are biases in even simple things like trying to adopt a cat or a dog. I’ll see ya then. Speaking of understanding how bias and misinformation spread, you should check out this video on Deep Fakes I did with Above the Noise -- another PBSDS channel that gets into the research behind controversial issues. Head over to the video in the description to find out how detect deep fakes. Tell them Jabril sent you! Crash Course AI is produced in association with PBS Digital Studios! If you want to help keep all Crash Course free for everybody, forever, you can join our community on Patreon. And if you want to learn more about prejudice and discrimination in humans, you can check out this episode of Crash Course Sociology.

- Algorithmic Bias in AI: What It Is and How to Fix It: Kind: captions Language: en The more we use AI algorithms to discover patterns, to generate insights and just to help us make decisions, the more we should be concerned with the impact of algorithmic bias. What is it and how can we minimize it? Well, let's find out. Algorithmic bias can lead to harmful decisions and actions, causing machine learning algorithms to produce unfair or discriminatory outcomes. It's something we want to avoid. So let's take a look at the causes of algorithmic bias, some real world examples and mitigation strategy, and let's get started with causes. Now algorithmic bias is not necessarily caused by the AI algorithms themselves, but by how data is collected and coded. We can think of this in terms of four different causes. Now, the most obvious is biases that occur in the actual training dataset itself. Essentially, we're talking about bad data. That's data that's non-representative or lacks information or is in some other way a misrepresentation of the ground truth. It can also be data that is incorrectly classified, causing the algorithm to misunderstand what the data represents, and a little bad data can go a long way. AI systems that generate biased results may use those results as input data for further decision making, and while that creates a feedback loop that can reinforce this bias over and over again. Now, another cause, of algorithm, of algorithmic bias is really related to algorithmic design. So this is talking about programing errors such as an eye designer unfairly weighting factors in the decision making process. They can unknowingly transfer into the system some of those biases, where it might be developers that might embed the algorithm with subjective rules based on their own conscious or unconscious biases. Poor algorithmic design that can also lead to correlation bias, such as an algorithm that determines a causal relationship between increased shark attacks and higher ice cream sales. Hey, they're both higher in the summer, but that's correlation, not causation, and an example of where the model failed to consider other factors in the data that may be of more importance. We can also have biases in proxy data as well. What's proxy data? Well, that's data used as a stand in for attributes not available in the ground truth data. So things like race or gender. And that could be because they're in some way protected or they just plain unavailable. For example, zip codes often serve as proxies for social economic status, that might unfairly disadvantage particular demographic groups when evaluating applications or opportunities. And there's also biases in evaluation as well. How we interpret the results from an algorithm. So even if the algorithm is completely neutral and it's completely data driven, how an individual or how a business applies the algorithms output can lead to unfair outcomes depending on how they understand those outputs. Now there are a bunch of real world examples of algorithmic bias. Look, I'm not here to name and shame, but let's briefly discuss a few high profile ones, like biases that have occurred in recruitment. Now an IT company built an algorithm, and that algorithm could review resumes. Unfortunately, they discovered this algorithm systematically discriminated against female job applicants. Why? Well, developers are training the hiring algorithm, use resumes from past hires, and it turns out that those past hires were predominantly male. As a result, the algorithm favored keywords and characteristics found in men's resumes. For example, the algorithm downgraded resumes that included the word women, as in women's rugby team, and it favored the kind of words that men tend to use more often, such as captured and executed. Now, algorithms, they also play a big role in guiding decisions in the area of finance. In the financial services sector and algorithmic bias here can have severe consequences for people's livelihoods, as historical data can contain all sorts of demographic biases affecting things like creditworthiness and loan approvals. For example, a study from the University of California, Berkeley showed that an AI system for mortgages routinely charges minority borrowers higher rates for the same loans when compared to white borrowers. And look, I could go on AI image generator, for example, where generated images of people in specialized professions found biases related to gender and age, or how bias in pricing led to ride sharing algorithms charging more for drop offs in neighborhoods with high nonwhite populations, or how policing algorithms in Columbia reflected social biases that misrepresented forecasted criminal activity, but how about we instead use the remaining time to figure out the steps that we can take to reduce algorithmic bias? Now mitigating bias from AI systems, that starts with AI governance. Many of the guardrails that make sure air tools and systems are safe and ethical. So let's take a look at four ways to do that across the system lifecycle. And first up is diverse and representative data. Machine learning is only as good as the data that trains it. Data fed into machine learning models must be representative of all groups of people and reflected of the actual demographics of society. Unlike, say, a training data set filled with only male resumes, but good representative data is just the start. There should also be a system for ongoing bias detection and that can detect and correct potential biases before they create problems. Now, that could be through initiatives like impact assessments, algorithmic auditing and causation tests. Remember sharks and ice cream? Now, this is where human in the loop processes can help, where recommendations be reviewed by humans before a decision is made final. Now the outputs of AI algorithms can often be something of a black box, making it difficult to understand their outcomes. So transparent AI those systems document and do their best to explain the underlying algorithms methodology. Now, to be clear, this is still an emerging field, but advances are being made in AI interpretability, which goes some way to explaining how algorithms arrive at their outcomes. And then finally, we have inclusive AI, which means developing AI systems where the developers, where the data scientists, where the machine learning engineers are varied racially, economically, by education level, by gender, by job description and all sorts of other demographic metrics This will bring different perspectives to help identify and mitigate biases that might otherwise go unnoticed. The fact is that algorithmic bias has many causes, and as AI becomes more prevalent in decision making, the importance of detecting and mitigating these biases only grows. If you have any questions, please drop us a line below. And if you want to see more videos like this in the future, please like and subscribe. Thanks for watching.

- Tech Bias and Algorithmic discrimination | Courtney Thomas Jr. | TEDxRochester: Kind: captions Language: en Since the 2016 election, there's been a lot of interest about what algorithmic discrimination is. And over the last year, I've had the opportunity to research how and when technological bias affects our daily lives and our social norms as a Kauffman Entrepreneurial Scholar at the University of Rochester. Algorithmic discrimination has the power to reinforce our innate prejudices and causes us to view the world in a divided context. The key is it can do this on such a wide scale and at such a rapid pace. Discrimination primarily manifests itself through the data that we use, the inputs that we allow computers to actually consider, and through the perpetuation of this black-box scenario, where we don't really know what the computer is doing to actually give us the answers to the questions we ask. But before we touch on those topics, it's important to make a relevant distinction in our conversation. Algorithms are not discriminatory, but they do produce the effect of discrimination. You see, all of us as humans are inherently biased. And our biases are completely natural, they're A-OK, but they do lead to cognitive bias, which is a systematic error in the way that we think about the world and treat the people in it. How many of you have little ones? You're not You're not proud of your little ones? There you go. I have little siblings, too. And I'll be the first to tell you that computers learn like kids. Just as we show our little ones how to go to the laboratory or the restroom over and over and over and over and over, and hope that they get it one day and go on their own. AI is very similar. We teach computers about inputs, and we show it what we want it to do over and over and over, and over and over and over. And eventually, the computer recognizes the input and acts upon it without a prompt. Easy, right? But a lot of computer scientists argue that methods like this and data mining eliminate human biases from AI decision-making processes. But an algorithm is only as good as the data that it uses and the data that it learns from. We're all familiar with that moment in life where we hit our toe against something and end up exclaiming something profane. If you do that in front of your little one, now they have a new favorite vocabulary word. That's because our speech is an input. And just as children mirror our behaviors, AI does, too. Even more so. AI takes our preferences as inputs and uses it to actually mimic our biases. It's not something that we actually want in our lives. See, some data is not good. Which essentially means it's imperfect, and it's imperfect in a way that allows the algorithms to inherit the biases of previous decision-makers. Training data can be imperfect in ways where it's not reflective of reality. It doesn't represent the context that we live in. For example, if a deep learning tool was shown more light-skinned faces than dark-skinned faces, then the resulting facial recognition system would inevitably be worse at recognizing dark-skinned faces. At the same time, this training data could also be representative of reality. And it can reflect the wide-scale biases that we have in society today, and that continues to persist. In this case, Amazon found its internal recruiting tool to be dismissing female candidates simply because it was trained with data that favored men over women, and it learned to do the same. Within this example, training data is not the only problem. It's also a problem of how the data was prepared. This includes considering what attributes of a candidate's application you want the AI or the algorithm to actually consider in its decision-making process. In the case of Amazon's recruiting tool, a candidate's gender, education level, years of work experience could all be considered attributes. This process of deep learning, choosing what attributes are considered and which are ignored, is oftentimes the most direct path to digital discrimination. An indirect path is also in the framing of our intent. Many times when computer scientists make algorithms, they're not thinking about unicorns and rainbows. They're thinking about what they want the actual model to achieve. If a credit card company might want to assess creditworthiness of a customer, but creditworthiness is a very nuanced concept. And in order to translate it into terms that the computer can actually understand, we dilute the holistic concepts that should be considered and turn those into objective statements like maximize profit. But if an AI found out that issuing subprime loans was an efficient way to maximize profit, then now our AI would be engaging in predatory behavior. Also something don't want. So again, I need your hands. For those of you have little ones, have you ever come home and figured that your little one has acquired a new skill? Right? Something that you have not taught them. Even though the skill might be entertaining and might be even helpful, you still have to ask that question of how'd you learn that? Or where did you get that from? Similar to cognitive heuristics and taking those mental shortcuts, we as humans are also just innately interested in the process of things. Sometimes we're not fortunate enough to know the process of things. And when our AI is engaging in predatory behaviors. A key challenge and a key barrier in the integration of AI into our daily lives is this lack of trust. And that's perpetuated through this black-box scenario, where we don't know how computers are actually making the decisions that we ask it to. If people don't know how decisions of their daily lives are being made, they ultimately won't trust it. This will lead to people who are already in marginalized groups having to face a new form and a new catalyst of oppression. In this chaotic Warring States era, killing never ceased, and a bleak, sorrowful atmosphere hung over the land. Qin, nominally the strongest state of the time, had already begun plotting to destroy the other six states and unify the realm. At this time, in Yongcheng, one of Qin's key military strongholds, there was stationed Qin's most elite army. In Li Family Village behind the mountain near Yongcheng, rain poured heavily from the sky. At that moment, Zhao Ji was kneeling in front of a grave, his face full of gloom and despair. Seeing this, Wan'er gently placed a hand on his shoulder and softly said, "Big Brother, Auntie has already passed away." She then moved to help Zhao Ji to his feet, but he stubbornly refused to leave. He said to Wan'er, "Wan'er, go back first. I'll be fine." The rain only deepened the chill in Zhao Ji's heart. Sadly, he reached out and touched the gravestone, lowering his head in pain as he murmured to himself, "I want to stay with Mother a little longer." The rain dripped down as his hand brushed over the neatly carved name of his mother on the wooden tombstone. He recalled his own origins. "I am Zhao Ji. Ever since I was born, I never knew who my father was." "And now Mother has left me too." Wan'er still had not moved a single step away. Heartbroken, she tried to persuade Zhao Ji. "If you're determined to torment yourself like this, then I'll kneel here with you too." And she did exactly as she said, kneeling on the ground beside him. Zhao Ji was stunned by what she had done, and he cried out in deep emotion. "Wan'er..." Wan'er answered resolutely, "I don't care. If Big Brother wants to kneel, then Wan'er will kneel with you too." Then she reached out and held the hand Zhao Ji had braced against the cold ground, as if to pass some strength to him. After a while, Zhao Ji slowly stood up and took Wan'er's hand to leave. The sky was dark and dim from the wind and rain, and the road back to Li Family Village at the foot of the mountain was slippery. Could there really be some major enemy target? Night gradually fell over the southern forest. Han’s secret route opened. The King of Han emerged with several others. Before them stood a group of Zhao soldiers who had come as reinforcements. This subordinate will escort you out of Xinzheng first.” Then he added, “This time, I will definitely escort you safely all the way to Handan.” The King of Han was escorted into the carriage, but before entering, he turned back and sighed, “With the General here, I am at ease.” Once everything was in order, Hu Nie waved his hand and gave the order to depart. At that exact moment, an arrow shot over and pierced straight through the center of his palm, making him cry out. It was the force led by Zhao Ji. On the side of the Yongcheng camp, Zhao Ji’s face was cold and impassive as he gave only one command: “Kill.” Bows were immediately raised and aimed at the Zhao troops. But service is limited to half a year. After six months, he may choose either to be discharged or to remain. There is no such thing as forced conscription.” General Tu Sui added, “In our Qin army, whether veteran or recruit, everyone receives stipends. If a man dies in battle, compensation is paid—enough to support his family.” Zhao Ji sat tapping the arm of the chair, then finally rose, clasping his hands behind his back as he said solemnly, “If what you said were true— that all Great Qin's soldiers were forced into service—then how could our army possibly maintain such strict discipline and remain undefeated? You truly have been blinded without even knowing it. Let me tell you one more thing. In Great Qin's army, there is no distinction of high and low. Everyone has a chance to become a marquis or a general. Kill the enemy and earn merit, and you can be granted rank. Under Great Qin's legal system, everyone is equal.” The Han soldiers still seemed unconvinced. The man asked suspiciously, “Looking across all the states, I've never heard of any legal system like that. You're exaggerating. Y-you want to trick us into losing face first and then kill us, don't you?” Zhao Ji raised his sword high and answered in a ringing voice, “That's exactly why I say you're frogs at the bottom of a well. Great Qin is undefeated because it has achieved what no other state can. And after hearing of Great Qin's legal system, you do not even dare to envy it. I, Zhao Ji, am valued by His Majesty and was appointed commander to suppress Han, placed over tens of thousands of troops. Yet just one year ago, I was only a poor disciple from an ordinary mountain village. I had no backing and no power. The position I hold today was earned through advancement through military merit. It was won by the sword in my hand that slew the enemy. In Great Qin, every soldier and officer is the same. This is something you Han people do not even dare dream of. It is also a grace that belongs only to the people of Great Qin.” After hearing all this, that Han soldier began to break down and fell to his knees on the ground, his hands clenched tight. “So we've been deceived by the whole world...” All the surrendered soldiers became dejected and sighed. “No wonder the soldiers and generals of Great Qin are so fierce. If I had that kind of chance to fight for my future, I too would be willing to risk my life. I only hate that I was born in Han. I also want to enlist under Qin.” Seeing this, Zhao Ji smiled inwardly. Psychological manipulation: successful. He stretched out his hand and used what he had already done to persuade them further. “If you too wish to serve Qin, then is the opportunity not right before your eyes? Han is finished. If you sincerely surrender to Qin, would you not become soldiers of Qin then?” The light of a firefly was tiny, but in darkness, even that faint glimmer was enough to make people scramble after it, treating it as hope regardless of the cost to themselves. Right now, these hundred thousand surrendered Han soldiers had been driven into a dead end. That only made them all the more eager to join the Qin army, and I am the lamp bringing them light, illuminating this darkness for them. Zhao Ji continued, “Under Great Qin's laws, there are only two kinds of judgment for those who surrender. One: become slaves and labor in the cities of Great Qin. Two: become convict soldiers and die on the battlefield protecting the Qin army in full. Both choices lead to only one ending: death. But today, I am giving you a completely different opportunity.” The surrendered Han soldiers began whispering among themselves. “Can we really become regular soldiers of Qin? We don't have to become slaves? Is that true or false?” Even Tu Sui was startled. He walked over to Zhao Ji and reminded him, “General, this has never been done before. Shouldn't you reconsider? If the higher-ups in Xianyang take notice, I fear His Majesty may censure you.” Zhao Ji smiled and said, “I am valued by His Majesty and stationed to guard Han territory. Naturally, I have full authority to decide.” Tu Sui answered, “But no matter what, they are still people of an enemy state.” Zhao Ji raised a hand to stop him and said, “The seven states are all of the same Yan and Yellow lineage. That is precisely why His Majesty harbors the ambition to unify them. Based on His Majesty's ambition, I am only changing the method for handling surrendered soldiers a little. I believe the King will surely approve. Even if one day His Majesty does censure me, I, this general, will bear all responsibility myself and not implicate anyone else.” Turning back toward the surrendered soldiers, he shouted, “You need only answer one thing: are you willing to serve Great Qin with all your heart and strength?” The Han soldiers shouted joyfully in unison, “General Zhao Ji is magnanimous and virtuous! We are willing to be loyal to Great Qin! We are willing to follow the General to the death!” Zhao Ji was delighted inwardly. A hundred thousand troops were now in his grasp. He waved his hand forward, and the surrendered soldiers immediately fell silent. Zhao Ji said, “Let me tell you this clearly. The chance I have given you—forgiveness, and the chance to become men of Great Qin's army—was a risky decision on my part. I hope you truly cherish it. You will only have this one chance. Serve Great Qin with all your heart. If any of you harbor thoughts of betrayal, your entire clan will be exterminated. There will absolutely be no pardon.” The surrendered Han soldiers all placed their hands over their chests and shouted together, “We will never be of two minds! We swear to be loyal to Great Qin unto death! Loyal to the General unto death! Please rest assured, General Zhao!” Zhao Ji turned around and instructed his two subordinates, “The two of you will immediately compile a full roster of the reserve troops. Incorporate them into the army under my command, but remember—break up their structure. Do not allow them to remain as one unified force.” The two men immediately cupped their hands. “This subordinate obeys.” Tu Sui turned to Zhang Han and said happily, “The General's move was truly brilliant. And bold as well. Just like that, he has taken in a hundred thousand surrendered soldiers.” Zhang Han replied, “In this world, only General Zhao would dare decide so decisively.” “And old Tu, this time our authority isn't just over fifty thousand troops anymore. Those hundred thousand surrendered soldiers have all been placed under us. As long as they swear loyalty to the General unto death, this is only the beginning.” Tu Sui nodded. “Exactly. As long as we follow the General, we will definitely be able to rise to even higher positions.” Up ahead, Zhao Ji lowered his eyes and thought to himself, These hundred thousand surrendered Han troops can now be used as my own. The strength under my control has already reached two hundred thousand. On future battlefields, the experience value the army can gain will be immeasurable. The Innate Realm is within reach. Back at his residence, when he saw a white horse standing before the gate, Zhao Ji froze. “That's a warhorse from the Meng family army. Why is it here?” He turned and asked the gate guard, “While I was away, did General Meng send someone?” Just as he was speaking, Pang Zhuang came running in. “Zhao Ji, you little brat, you've sinned badly!” Zhao Ji was at once embarrassed. “Why are you here?” He felt guilty inside. Could it be that they already knew about his pardon of the surrendered soldiers and had come to call him to account? Pang Zhuang put a hand on his tightly clenched fist and said, “Zhao Ji, this time I've come on behalf of the two generals of the Meng family army to teach you a lesson. Do you know your crime yet?” Zhao Ji smiled and replied, “Brother Pang, explain it first. What exactly have I done?” Pang Zhuang immediately slung an arm around his neck. “Brat, when you registered for military service, you declared yourself unmarried. But not only did you take Li Si's daughter, you even got her pregnant. If I hadn't gone to Li Family Village, how much longer were you planning to keep this hidden?” Zhao Ji was stunned and quickly explained, “It is true that I have a childhood sweetheart who is my betrothed, but we were not formally engaged yet. Besides, she isn't Li Si's daughter.” Pang Zhuang frowned. “You really know nothing at all? You're not pretending to be stupid with me, are you?” “Then you'd better steady yourself. Don't get too excited. This is a personal letter from General Meng. Read it yourself.” As he spoke, he handed over a bamboo slip. Zhao Ji replied boldly, “So mysterious. I wasn't even afraid when I beheaded the King of Han. What could possibly make me lose my composure?” He took the bamboo slip. But the moment his eyes swept over its contents, it fell to the ground. Zhao Ji stared as though he could not believe his eyes. “I... I have children? Yuan'er gave birth to dragon-phoenix twins for me?” Pang Zhuang burst out laughing. “Hahaha! You lucky brat.” Zhao Ji was instantly overjoyed. The dream had become reality. In these troubled times, Yuan'er had borne his flesh and blood. Yuan'er, your useless brother promised to bring you happiness and safety, yet I wasn't by your side when you needed me most. He immediately rushed off in a hurry, shouting as he ran, “Li Qing, prepare a horse! I have to return to Li Family Village!” Pang Zhuang chased after him, calling out, “Huh? Why the rush?” “A round trip between Li Family Village and Xinzheng takes a whole month. No matter what, you should at least hand over the affairs in the city first.” Zhao Ji suddenly stopped. Pang Zhuang was bewildered. “What is it?” Zhao Ji turned back and replied, “Good thing you reminded me. I really was muddle-headed. Han territory has only just stabilized, and the surrounding states are watching like hungry tigers. If I, the commanding general, leave now, chaos will definitely break out.” He thought to himself that in that dream, there was not only happiness, but also swords and spears. If something happened in Han territory, he would certainly be punished. Not only would all his past efforts go to waste, but in his current immature state, he might even lose his life. And if that happened, how could he possibly speak of giving Yuan'er a safe and secure life? Pang Zhuang looked admiring. “You really do think things through. I almost made a huge mistake.” He put a hand on Zhao Ji's shoulder and comforted him. “But don't worry too much. As soon as General Meng learned that your wife had given birth, he immediately arranged everything properly. He even submitted a memorial to His Majesty. Given your current status, the King will soon bestow rewards as well. So don't worry about your wife.” Zhao Ji replied, “General Meng handled this very thoroughly.” He thought to himself, General Meng's actions not only protected Yuan'er, they also helped me take another step forward and gain the trust of Ying Zheng. He then knelt before Pang Zhuang. “Brother Pang, I will never forget the debt I owe you all. Please thank the two Generals Meng on my behalf for taking care of her.” Pang Zhuang quickly reached out and pulled him up. “Get up. Saying such things between brothers is going too far.” Zhao Ji stood up and said, “It's just that I truly never imagined Yuan'er was Li Si's daughter. Then when Yuan'er gave birth this time, did Li Si not know?” Pang Zhuang turned his head away, hesitating a little. “About that... I didn't want to tell you, for fear you'd worry. But sooner or later you'll find out anyway. More than six months ago, Li Si drove your wife out of the family home. If the people of Li Family Village hadn't helped your wife, then let alone giving birth safely—even surviving would have been difficult.” Zhao Ji's face changed at once. “What? Yuan'er is his own flesh and blood. How could he be so cruel?” Pang Zhuang replied, “I heard that back then, Li Si wanted to marry into Young Master Fusu's family. He wanted to marry his daughter to him and become in-laws, and even the King had already approved it. But who would have thought you'd get there first? Because of that, Li Yuan'er would rather die than submit to the marriage.” “In the end, Li Si was provoked into anger and humiliation, so he drove her out of the household and left her to fend for herself.” Zhao Ji silently engraved the hatred in his heart. Li Si, I had thought that for Yuan'er's sake, I would let you off. I never expected... Seeing the hatred all over Zhao Ji's face, Pang Zhuang was afraid he might do something rash and hurriedly warned him, “Hey, Zhao, you have to stay calm. When it comes to this kind of matter, you absolutely must not act impulsively. Li Si is currently favored by the King. If you set yourself against him, your road to advancement will definitely be obstructed.” Zhao Ji smiled and said, “Thank you. I know my limits.” But that last sentence—This grudge, I will remember—he said only in his heart. Zhao Ji returned to his room and said, “I can't go back myself, so I'll have to trouble you to deliver a letter to my home for me, and help set Yuan'er's mind at ease.” Pang Zhuang answered, “That'll do.” He then took up a brush and wrote on a bamboo slip: “Yuan'er, my wife, you have suffered because of me. I never once expected you to become pregnant unexpectedly, and that our children would enter this world safely. I, Zhao Ji, am neither talented nor virtuous, yet I have been blessed with such great fortune. Rest assured—for your sake, and even more for the sake of our children, I will do everything in my power to fight for the future that belongs to us. I will also return to you as soon as possible. Wait for me.” After finishing, he handed the letter to Pang Zhuang. “Old Pang, you've been troubled this time. I should really have kept you here for a few days.” Pang Zhuang mounted his horse and turned back from the great gate. “Hahaha, I understand, I understand. But kid, consider this a debt you owe me.” With that, he spurred his horse and rode away. Then a voice came from behind Zhao Ji. “The man just now looked like he was wearing General Meng's armor.” Zhao Ji turned around and saw two men approaching. “Lord Feng, Young Master Han.” “That was indeed General Pang Zhuang of the Meng family army just now. He came to bring me news that my fiancée had given birth safely. Since it was a private matter, I did not report it to Lord Feng.” Feng Quji smiled and said, “So that was it. Congratulations, General Zhao, on gaining noble offspring. By rights, General Meng should now be hurrying back to Xianyang to report on the situation. I thought perhaps, before he left, General Zhao had some instructions to pass on, and so had sent someone ahead.” Zhao Ji replied, “Pang Zhuang never mentioned anything about the Meng family army going to Xianyang. If Lord Feng had not said so, I would not have known.” He thought to himself, There is hidden meaning in his words. As expected of a loyal minister of Ying Zheng. Zhao Ji then asked, “May I ask where Lord Feng and Young Master Han are headed?” Feng Quji answered, “When I came here, I had to send a regular memorial to His Majesty, so before going to Young Master Han's camp, I came to inspect the surrendered soldiers.” Zhao Ji immediately felt a trace of suspicion. I only just pardoned the surrendered troops, and Feng Quji immediately proposes sending up a memorial. After all, this does violate Qin law. Could it be that Feng Quji does not understand the pros and cons and wants to accuse me? Han Fei seemed to understand what he meant and shook his head behind Feng Quji. Zhao Ji let out a sigh, apparently everything was fine. I still have Han Fei, my trump card, in hand. Li Si, one day I will drag you down from power and make you pay for your mistakes. A month later, a horse carriage drove in outside Zhangtai Palace. Resentful curses came from inside the carriage, “Hmph, how dare he overturn the laws of our Qin dynasty. Granting a mass pardon to the surrendered Han soldiers—Zhao Ji, oh Zhao Ji. No matter how great your achievements are, this time you’re dead for sure.” As he spoke, Li Si tightened his grip on the scroll in his hand. He turned toward the carriage door and asked his attendant, “Has Feng Quji’s memorial definitely been delivered to Zhangtai Palace?” “This is merely borrowing a knife to kill.” The attendant immediately replied, “Yes, my lord. But His Majesty has already bestowed a marriage upon Zhao Ji and Miss Yuan’er. Miss Yuan’er has even given birth to a pair of twins. Do you truly intend to move against Zhao Ji?” Li Si said calmly, “So what? Not to mention that unfilial girl Li Yuan caused me to lose my chance to become in-laws with Young Master Fusu. Zhao Ji has opposed me time and again. The two of us have long been like fire and water. How could I possibly spare him? Wu Da went to Han territory and then vanished, and afterward Han Fei even became an official of Great Qin—more than half of these matters were orchestrated by him alone.” Gnashing his teeth, he said, “If I am merciful and tolerant, will I still have any place left in Great Qin in the future or not? But if I want to completely bring Zhao Ji down, I must first make Meng Wu keep silent. This time he has returned to Xianyang to report on the situation. If I accuse Zhao Ji, he will naturally obstruct me.” As they proceeded deeper into the palace, another group blocked Li Si’s way. From within the crowd came a loud shout, “Hey! Old man Huan Yi, still refusing to admit defeat?” Huan Yi immediately retorted, “Who admitted defeat? Who are you calling a coward?” Huan Yi and Meng Wu were using all their strength to arm-wrestle. Li Si stepped forward and asked, “My lords, what is this?” “Reporting to Lord Li Si, General Meng Wu and General Huan Yi are always like this. The moment they meet, it’s as if swords are drawn and bows are bent. Today His Majesty has summoned them, and since it isn’t appropriate for them to spar, they decided to arm-wrestle instead.” Li Si said, “So that’s how it is.” On the table, one hand had already been forced down by the other. Meng Wu stood up, cracked his knuckles, and laughed mockingly. “Hahaha, Old Huan, you lost. Life in Lantian has been too comfortable, hasn’t it? Even your strength has weakened.” Huan Yi angrily shouted at Meng Wu, “Stop flapping your gums. If you’ve got the guts, compete in something else.” Meng Wu laughed and replied, “His Majesty has summoned us. I don’t want to be scolded by him for looking disheveled either. Besides, a loss is a loss. Even if I compete with you again, wouldn’t it just end the same way? Ah, that feels great. I’ll be going first.” As he spoke, Meng Wu turned and left, leaving behind a furious Huan Yi shouting after him, “You damned old bastard, just you wait!” Li Si then stepped forward with a smile and said, “General Huan, don’t be angry. General Meng Wu is rather pleased with himself at the moment, so just let him go.” Huan Yi turned to him and frowned. “What do you mean?” Li Si replied, “You two are both among the finest military generals of Great Qin, and both serve the court with complete devotion. His Majesty has always regarded you as equals. But I’m afraid the situation may soon change. The one receiving the most attention right now is Zhao Ji. He comes from Yongcheng and is also highly regarded by General Meng Wu. If Zhao Ji continues to rise after this audience, then General Meng Wu’s influence at court could be said to become unrivaled. At that point, General Huan Yi, your position... hahaha...” As he spoke, he turned to Huan Yi with a meaningful smile. He thought to himself, In the end, he’s just a simple-minded military man. Just obediently help me deal with Meng Wu. No one Li Si wants dead has ever survived, and Zhao Ji will be no exception. Inside the main hall, all the ministers bowed in salute. “Your servants pay respects to the King.” Seated upon the throne above, the King of Qin waved his hand to excuse the ceremony. At that moment Li Si felt very pleased with himself. Meng Wu, even if you protect him, Zhao Ji is doomed this time. The King of Qin above spoke, “A few days ago, Feng Quji submitted a memorial regarding Han territory. What are your views?” Li Si stepped into the center of the hall, cupped his hands, and said, “Your Majesty, Zhao Ji, commander stationed in Han territory, is unworthy of royal favor. He violated the laws of Great Qin and arbitrarily granted a mass pardon to surrendered soldiers, acting with reckless audacity. I earnestly ask Your Majesty to investigate.” From behind him, Meng Wu refuted, “Everything Li Si says is sophistry. Although Zhao Ji’s methods differ from precedent, our laws of Qin also stipulate that slaves who render meritorious service to the state may be pardoned. Then what crime has Zhao Ji committed?” Li Si turned and said with a smile, “General Zhao Ji mixed the surrendered soldiers into the roster of our Qin troops and even gave them stipends, increasing financial expenditures. That is his grave offense.” Meng Wu frowned. “May I ask the Commandant of Justice, in the months since Zhao Ji took up his post, have you heard that Han territory has been poorly managed or run into financial difficulties? If not, then that proves Zhao Ji’s decision was not flawed. Lord Li Si does not understand military governance, so you should refrain from talking too much lest you embarrass yourself.” Li Si flew into a rage and pointed at Meng Wu. “Em-embarrass myself! You—how can you, as a great minister, be so rude in court?” Meng Wu crossed his arms and said calmly, “I am a military man. If anything I say is improper, I trust His Majesty will be lenient.” He then turned upward and cupped his hands to the King of Qin. “Your Majesty, Zhao Ji’s success in making the surrendered soldiers submit is a great achievement. I ask Your Majesty to reward Zhao Ji.” Li Si immediately cut in, “Your Majesty, do not listen to General Meng Wu. Zhao Ji comes from Yongcheng, so of course he is biased in his favor. General Huan Yi is also a great general. Why not ask what he thinks as well?” The King of Qin nodded. “Reasonable. General Huan Yi, you come from Lantian. In your opinion, should Zhao Ji be punished or rewarded?” Huan Yi cupped his hands and replied, “Your Majesty, Zhao Ji’s actions were indeed bold.” Li Si snorted inwardly. Huan Yi and Meng Wu are like fire and water—completely incompatible. He will naturally stand on my side. At Huan Yi’s side, however, he continued, “But this method not only fundamentally solves the limitations in dealing with rebellious surrendered troops, it also expands Great Qin’s military strength. Therefore, I believe this method should be promoted throughout the Qin army of Great Qin.” Li Si looked up, his face changing color. “Wh-what?” After hearing Huan Yi’s opinion, General Meng Wu was extremely gratified. He patted Huan Yi on the chest and praised him, “Haha, Old Huan, I’ll count it that you do have some discernment.” Huan Yi still looked somewhat sulky as he replied, “Hmph. I’m doing this for Great Qin, not speaking for you.” Having said that, Meng Wu shot Li Si an angry look. He rejoiced inwardly: Hahaha, Li Si, oh Li Si, you’re narrow-minded and selfish. Did you really think Huan Yi and I were enemies? You truly underestimate our loyalty to Great Qin. Besides, both Huan Yi and I cherish talent. How could we possibly join hands with you to frame a capable general like Zhao Ji? The King of Great Qin was also rather pleased. He replied to the ministers below, “I already understand what my ministers mean, and I have made my decision.” Holding the memorial in his hand, he read it solemnly and gave his view. The King continued, “In Feng Quji’s memorial, Zhao Ji says, ‘The seven states are all of the same Yan and Huang lineage; therefore, the ambition to unify them is truly a most fair-minded sentiment,’ and these words have won my heart as well.” Upon hearing this, the ministers below immediately broke into discussion. “General Zhao Ji not only devises plans for warfare, I never expected him to understand the realm so deeply as well. What a talented man.” Another minister also strongly agreed, saying, “Very well said. The realm is vast and the states stand firm, yet we are all of the same Yan and Huang lineage.” Someone else voiced his agreement as well. “For such an outstanding man to serve as a general of Great Qin is truly a blessing for Qin.” A moment later, the King rose with imperial bearing and declared, “Zhao Ji said he was willing to bear punishment alone when introducing a new method—this is great righteousness. With a single statement he subdued one hundred thousand surrendered troops in Han territory—this is wisdom. Such character, bearing, and insight truly do not disappoint me.” All the ministers below spoke in unison, “Your Majesty is wise!” Then the King looked toward Li Si and said to him, “Furthermore, Feng Quji reports that Han Fei was recommended by Zhao Ji and has now surrendered to Great Qin. With his help, Han territory is gradually coming under Qin’s control. This is yet another merit.” Then the King’s expression turned stern as he rebuked Li Si. “Commandant of Justice Li Si, though you hold high office, you cannot distinguish talent. Your vision is too biased, and that disappoints me.” Li Si hurriedly bowed and admitted his fault. “Your Majesty, please forgive me. I only wished to safeguard the laws of Great Qin. Heaven and earth may witness my loyalty.” Seeing Li Si in this state, General Meng Wu could not help feeling satisfied. He said to Li Si, “Lord Li Si, in the future you should simply do your own job well. Overstepping your authority and trying to meddle in military and political affairs is truly laughable.” The King continued issuing orders. “I have entrusted the military affairs of Han territory to Zhao Ji. I trust him. All matters in the army are under Zhao Ji’s authority to decide. If something like this happens again in the future, there is no need to make such a fuss.” The King looked rather troubled as he continued, “At present, Wang Jian is guarding the border against two states. Zhao and Wei may not dare to act rashly, but their troops have still not withdrawn. I suspect they will secretly make a move against Han territory. Great Qin will very soon be at war again. Fortunately, Han territory has Zhao Ji, which puts my mind somewhat at ease.” Then the King again ordered the ministers, “Ministers, Han has already been destroyed by our Great Qin. Next will be Zhao and Wei. Just as Zhao Ji said—unify the world. Whoever dares obstruct my unification of the descendants of Yan and Huang shall be killed without mercy.” Everyone below shouted in unison, “Your Majesty is wise! We are willing to follow Your Majesty unto death and help Great Qin unify the world!” Seeing everyone united in support, the King felt the matter was settled and prepared to leave. “If there is nothing further today, then all of you may withdraw.” Just when it seemed everything had been dealt with, Li Si suddenly called out, “Your Majesty, this minister still has one more matter. My daughter Li Yuan’er received the sacred favor of being betrothed to Zhao Ji, yet the two have still not held their marriage ceremony. Now my daughter is living in Li Family Village. I earnestly beg Your Majesty to allow me to bring her and her children back to Xianyang so that I may conveniently care for them.” As he made this request, Li Si was already harboring another vicious thought. If he could not kill Zhao Ji, then at the very least he had to seize Zhao Ji’s weakness in his own hands. Li Si continued pleading, “I ask Your Majesty to fulfill this father’s longing for his daughter.” Sensing the problem in Li Si’s request, General Meng Wu grew worried. Well played, Li Si. Since you failed to frame Zhao Ji, now you’ve turned your attention to your own daughter. At once, General Meng Wu immediately addressed the King. “Your Majesty, that must absolutely not be allowed. If Li Si is permitted to bring Li Yuan’er back, it will be hard to guarantee the safety of her and her children.” At this, Li Si hurriedly explained himself while reproaching Meng Wu. “General Meng, you are truly unreasonable. I am her father. I want to bring my daughter and grandchildren home. What could possibly be wrong with that?” General Huan Yi also chimed in, “Come on, Old Meng, this is their family matter. Don’t meddle.” But General Meng Wu still earnestly implored the King, “Your Majesty, please hear me out.” He did his utmost to explain to the King, “At first, Li Yuan’er and Zhao Ji loved each other, but Li Si kept clinging to Young Master Fusu and forcibly separated them. Later, when Li Yuan’er would rather die than marry someone else, Li Si drove her out of the house and left her to fend for herself. Long ago he already severed the relationship between father and daughter. Your Majesty, if Li Yuan’er had not been taken in and cared for by the kind villagers of Li Family Village, I fear she would have perished unjustly by now. How can she possibly be delivered into a tiger’s jaws once again?” After hearing this, the King cried out in alarm, “What?” General Meng Wu continued presenting evidence. “Moreover, Zhao Ji is currently guarding Han territory. The states of Zhao and Wei are eyeing it like hungry tigers. If he learns that Li Yuan’er is being coerced by Li Si, how can Zhao Ji possibly devote himself wholeheartedly to resisting the enemy?” Seeing Meng Wu expose Li Si’s crimes like this, even General Huan Yi could no longer hold back. He also berated Li Si to his face. “Li Si, you actually dared do such a thing? You are unworthy of being a man, much less a father.” The weak-voiced Li Si tried to explain, “H-hey, don’t just spout nonsense.” But General Meng Wu cut him off at once. “Your Majesty, every word I have spoken is true. The villagers of Li Family Village can testify to all of it.” Li Si angrily retorted, “You’re sticking your nose into my family affairs. General Meng, you’re meddling too broadly.” General Meng firmly protected Zhao Ji and replied, “As long as this general is here, no one is allowed to harm Zhao Ji or his family—including you.” Hearing both sides arguing, the King above was getting a headache from the noise. In a mild voice, the King ordered, “Enough. Stop making such a clamor.” Then the King gave his ruling on the matter. “I do not wish to interfere too much, but what I dislike most is breaking apart lovers. Li Si, you once forcibly separated Zhao Ji and Li Yuan’er, and afterward abandoned your own daughter. That was truly disgraceful.” Li Si stammered in fear, “Y-your servant knows his crime.” Then Li Si immediately knelt in the hall and begged forgiveness. The King issued his order to Li Si. “You will personally go to find Li Yuan’er and see whether she is willing to return to your residence with you. This matter depends entirely on her wishes. You are not to force her. And even if Li Yuan’er does return, she and her children must be placed under General Meng Wu’s protection.” Having said that, the weary King departed. “I am tired. If there is nothing else, all of you may withdraw.” Thus the ministers left, and only General Meng Wu remained behind. Seeing this, the King found it strange and asked, “Minister Meng, is there something else?” Only then did Meng Wu slowly report, “Yes, Your Majesty, I still have a private matter.” General Meng Wu began speaking to the King. “Your Majesty, did you once have a jade pendant that you were especially fond of? Do you still have it now?” The King asked in confusion, “A jade pendant? What jade pendant?” Seeing this, Meng Wu laughed it off. “Ahaha. Perhaps this minister remembered wrongly. Please pretend I said nothing. I take my leave.” The King still stood there, baffled. “This Meng Wu—at his age, and still so rash and careless.” But then the King fell into thought again. A jade pendant? Why did Meng Wu suddenly ask about that? Back then I took my most beloved jade pendant and gave it to Dong’er. Could it be that Meng Wu has seen Dong’er? But Meng Wu knows her—perhaps it was only a coincidence. Then the King slowly walked away, looking up at the blue sky as he remembered the woman he had loved in years past. “My Dong’er, back then only because of the twists of fate in our family circumstances were you and I forced apart. But now I have become a king above tens of thousands. Where are you now? Dong’er, your Brother Zheng has grown up. I can protect you now.
