Seeing this scene, Tu Sui also fell into thought for a moment. “Today, many of the former Han reserve troops will become regular soldiers of Great Qin.” “And what is most precious is that, seeing them speak to one another without any distance between them, it proves they submitted long ago.” With that, Tu Sui began gathering the soldiers. “Men, gather your strength and prepare for battle! If we’re acting, then we act to the end. In a moment, throw away your armor and run.” All the soldiers shouted in unison, “Yes!” Then, from atop the city wall, Tu Sui ordered his men, “Let’s make a big harvest. Fire the arrows!” Hundreds of flaming arrows shot forth at once, streaking straight toward the Zhao-Wei army. The Zhao-Wei soldiers struck by the fire arrows fell like straw. As the flames spread, Pang Nuan and his subordinates stood still and watched the brutal scene, yet they remained calm, believing the city could still be taken. Beneath the city wall, the Zhao-Wei soldiers hurriedly set up ladders and climbed the wall. Above them, Tu Sui continued shouting to his soldiers, “With the catapults covering us, charge, men!” Pang Nuan saw that they had already climbed up to the city gate, and he cried out in delight, “Success! We’ve succeeded!” One of Pang Nuan’s subordinates quickly reported the good news to him. “Reporting to General, our army has successfully climbed onto the walls of Nanyang!” After hearing that, Pang Nuan urgently ordered, “Quick, prepare the battering ram for me!” Following Pang Nuan’s order, his soldiers dragged out a huge, sharp-tipped battering ram for smashing the gate. They shouted, “Storm the city! Break down the gate!” The soldiers surged forward like a storm and launched a fierce assault on Nanyang’s gate. The pointed head of the ram slammed violently into the gate. Once, twice—the massive ram pounded hard against the center of the gate. Thick battle smoke rose everywhere. After a while, one of Tu Sui’s subordinates reported, “General Tu Sui, everything has been prepared.” At that very moment, the battering ram broke open the gates of Nanyang. Zhao-Wei soldiers poured into the city. “Nanyang has fallen! Kill them!” “Kill!” Tu Sui calmly gave one short order: “Withdraw.” The Zhao-Wei troops were still full of momentum. “Kill! Kill!” Pang Nuan ordered his men to leave ten thousand cavalry to guard the supplies. “The whole army, move out! Wipe out the remnants inside the city and destroy tyrannical Qin for me!” After a while, one of Pang Nuan’s subordinates reported the situation to him. “Reporting to Supreme General, all our troops have entered the city. The Great Qin army has fled in complete disorder. Nanyang City is now under our control.” But Supreme General Pang Nuan cared only about Zhao Ji. He asked whether the Qin commander had been captured alive. “What are the Qin army’s casualties?” The subordinate froze, then answered hesitantly, “Reporting to General, we have not found the Qin commander, and not a single Qin soldier casualty has been discovered. When our army stormed the city, the Qin troops had already all fled. Moreover, there is not even a trace of the common people inside. Nanyang is now an empty city.” After hearing this, Pang Nuan was shocked and alarmed. “What?” He immediately realized something was definitely wrong. He hurriedly ordered, “This is bad! We’ve fallen into their trap! The whole army, retreat at once—leave the city now!” The subordinate still did not understand and asked, “Supreme General, what do you mean?” Before Pang Nuan could explain, hundreds of blazing arrows suddenly flew toward where they were standing. Pang Nuan’s group staggered in shock, not knowing how to respond, and everyone shouted in panic to one another: “There’s an ambush! There’s lamp oil on the rooftops!” That was right—Great Qin soldiers were standing on the roofs of the houses, firing flaming arrows downward to exterminate the Zhao-Wei troops. The Zhao-Wei soldiers rushed to flee. “Heavens! The Qin army didn’t run at all! They’re setting the city on fire! Quick, retreat!” But some of them quickly discovered, “This is bad! The city gates have been shut! We can’t get out! There’s fire everywhere! Save me! I don’t want to die!” Nanyang City erupted in towering flames. The raging fire trapped the Zhao-Wei soldiers inside, and one after another, they were swallowed by the flames. Zhao Ji, Tu Sui, and Zhang Han sat calmly on horseback outside the city, watching the Zhao-Wei soldiers burn alive. A moment later, Zhao Ji moved his horse as if he intended to ride into the blaze. Zhang Han quickly asked in confusion, “General, where are you going?” Zhao Ji answered calmly, “I’m going to meet Supreme General Pang Nuan.” Tu Sui anxiously tried to stop him. “But General, at every city gate and every exit of Nanyang, I arranged thornwood and fire devices according to your orders.” After hearing that, Zhao Ji showed not the slightest fear and replied with a smile, “Didn’t I tell you to reduce the firepower at the rear gate of Nanyang? That was precisely to leave him a path to survive.” At that moment inside Nanyang, Pang Nuan’s soldiers were still screaming miserably, “Help! It’s too hot! It hurts! Qin army, spare us!” A few loyal soldiers still shouted, “Even in life or death, we must protect the Supreme General!” These men drew their swords and fought with all their strength to protect him. And Young Master Wei Tai broke out of the encirclement. “Charge out! Charge out!” Supreme General Pang Nuan could only sigh helplessly and blame himself. “I am ashamed before the soldiers of Great Zhao who died so tragically. I am a sinner of Zhao and of the Three Jin. I deserve death.” Under the desperate cover of his subordinates, Supreme General Pang Nuan was finally escorted safely to the rear gate of Nanyang. Young Master Wei Tai cried out joyfully, “We got out!” But before he could stay happy for even three seconds, his face instantly changed, pale with fear and covered in sweat. “Ah—it’s the Qin army!” Standing right before Young Master Wei Tai was Zhao Ji’s imposing force, already waiting for them. Seeing that Pang Nuan’s group had escaped exactly as he had planned, Zhao Ji said calmly, “Pang Nuan, this general has been waiting for you here for a long time.” Young Master Wei Tai shouted, “Y-you, who are you?” Supreme General Pang Nuan quickly cut him off. “Hahaha, how muddleheaded! With such schemes and methods, who else could it be but Zhao Ji, commander of the Great Qin army?” Hearing Pang Nuan say this, Wei Tai could not help but panic. “But wasn’t Zhao Ji already dead?” Pang Nuan remained fairly calm as he explained, “That was only a trick to deceive the enemy. We are all fish in the pot now.” Zhao Ji leapt down from his horse in high spirits and replied, “To have my name known by Zhao’s Supreme General is a great honor for this general!” Pang Nuan now angrily questioned Zhao Ji. “You set fire to Nanyang! More than a hundred thousand of our Zhao-Wei troops have been burned alive. Zhao Ji, your scheme is truly good—very good indeed. And your methods are vicious as well. No wonder you bear the title of Little God of Slaughter.” Zhao Ji only answered indifferently, “War has always been like this.” Then Zhao Ji pressed him forcefully: “I respect you as Zhao’s Supreme General, so I will ask only one question. Will you fight, or surrender?” Supreme General Pang Nuan merely drew his sword and assumed a posture to kill himself, answering loudly, “A single oversight from me ruined the whole army. You schemed for an entire month, and only when I entered the city did I see through even a little of it.” “I am truly useless. Even in death I have no regrets!” Pang Nuan raised his sword forward, offering it to Zhao Ji, and said, “I have heard that General Zhao treats prisoners well. I, Pang Nuan, am willing to exchange my death for the lives of the soldiers under my command.” But Zhao Ji replied, “You alone are not enough. Zhao and Wei offended the heavenly might of Great Qin, so naturally I must also take the life of the supreme commander of the Zhao-Wei forces.” Young Master Wei Tai was horrified and frightened. “What? N-no, I don’t want to die! I don’t want to die!” Seeing the other man’s cowardly reaction, Pang Nuan frowned and rebuked him, “General Wei, as military men, the two of us should long since have treated life and death lightly. Now that our army has been defeated, what is wrong with using our two deaths to buy the lives of the soldiers under our command?” But Wei Tai would not listen. Terrified, he lashed his horse hard with the whip and tried to flee. He retorted to Pang Nuan, “What do you mean, treat life and death lightly? I can’t die. I am a prince of Great Wei. If I die, Great Wei will have no heir!” Then he shouted orders to his soldiers, “Soldiers of Great Wei, obey me! Break out with this young master, now!” Then Wei Tai fled under the escort of his own troops. Supreme General Pang Nuan could only stand there and watch that coward run off. Seeing this, Zhang Han hurriedly ordered the archers to ready themselves. But Zhao Ji raised his hand in time, signaling them to stop. He said to Zhang Han, “Wait. Even if we shoot ten thousand arrows, there will still surely be fish that slip through the net.” Then he told Zhang Han how to catch the fish. “We only need to catch the one at the head.” Zhao Ji then raised his bow and prepared to strike at Wei Tai. The cowardly and irresponsible Young Master Wei Tai, his face purple with fear, spurred his horse and fled. The horse ran farther and farther, while Zhao Ji had already drawn his bow and taken careful aim, ready to shoot. In a flash, an iron arrow flew toward Wei Tai. With Zhao Ji’s divine archery, the result was easy to predict. The arrow pierced straight into Wei Tai’s body. He cried out in pain, lost his grip on the reins, and was nearly thrown from his horse. Seeing that his arrow had struck true, Zhao Ji used it as a warning. “Let this arrow be an example to the remnant troops of Zhao and Wei. Whoever still runs about in disorder will meet the same end as him.” Supreme General Pang Nuan was astonished. Seeing Zhao Ji’s skill with the bow, he could not help but sigh inwardly, “From over a hundred zhang away, General Zhao killed his target with a single arrow.” Zhao Ji then said to Pang Nuan, “Though he is of the royal clan, he has disgraced the dignity of royalty. In contrast, General Pang, you truly bear the bearing of a great general.” Pang Nuan still gripped the sword tightly in his hand and said in a low voice, “One arrow shook the entire remnant army. I, Pang Nuan, am convinced in both heart and speech.” Zhao Ji walked up before Pang Nuan, lifted the sword, and said to him, “This general agrees to your request for surrender and will spare the lives of the soldiers under your command. Before you die, is there anything you wish to say?” Only then did Supreme General Pang Nuan begin to feel regret for himself. He said, “I can only lament that Heaven is too unfair. Why was a talented general like you, General Zhao, born in tyrannical Qin rather than in my Great Zhao?” But Zhao Ji’s next words truly shook Pang Nuan. Zhao Ji said, “Even if I had been born in Zhao, I still would have surrendered. With my background, no matter how capable I was, in Zhao I would only have been an unknown common soldier. And the King of Zhao does not possess the grand talent and mighty vision needed to unite all under Heaven.” Supreme General Pang Nuan was truly thrown into confusion. Feeling this was improper, he argued back, “Tyrannical Qin destroys the other states and still dreams of building a flourishing age for all under Heaven? That will bring only hatred!” Zhao Ji did not care. He turned away and answered calmly, “General Pang Nuan, you truly are stubborn. I will make you sincerely convinced—consider it my sign of respect for you.” With that, Zhao Ji shouted, “Where are the surrendered soldiers of Han?” Hearing their commander’s call, all the Han soldiers who had surrendered to Great Qin raised their swords high and shouted, “Long live the commander!” Their overwhelming momentum alone was enough to inspire awe. Zhao Ji continued loudly, “Are you now soldiers of Han, or warriors of my Great Qin?” All the soldiers answered in unison, “We swear to serve Great Qin unto death! We swear to serve Great Qin unto death!” They shouted it again and again for Pang Nuan to witness. Then Zhao Ji turned to him and said, “You kept sending men to contact Han’s defeated troops to coordinate from within and without during the siege, yet no one responded. Isn’t that right?” Pang Nuan was left speechless, because it was exactly true. The surrendered Han soldiers continued shouting before Zhao Ji, “We swear to serve Great Qin unto death! We swear to serve Great Qin unto death!” The whole army swore loyalty to their commander and to Great Qin. The sword was still pressed against Pang Nuan’s neck as Zhao Ji continued to enlighten him: “This is exactly why those defeated remnants are now soldiers of my Great Qin. Once the other five states are destroyed, the soldiers and people of the other lands will likewise be unified into Great Qin.” Supreme General Pang Nuan answered sorrowfully, “Perhaps you are right. But you are still so young, and you have already rendered great service. Have you ever thought about being discarded once the bridge has been crossed?” Zhao Ji only coldly slashed with his sword in a flash. He thought to himself, “You’re about to die, and you still want to sow discord? If you were not Zhao’s Supreme General—worth experience points and generous rewards—I really would have wanted to keep you alive to watch what comes later.” After dealing with Pang Nuan, Zhao Ji patted his saddle and prepared to mount and leave. Sitting proudly in the saddle, he raised his sword high and shouted, “Warriors of Great Qin, Pang Nuan has been slain by this general! Great Qin has won this battle!” The soldiers below cheered gratefully. “The General is divinely mighty! The General is awe-inspiring in war!” Zhao Ji was exhilarated and deeply satisfied. Smiling brightly at everyone, he thought to himself, “Pang Nuan wasn’t wrong. With such great merit this time, the King of Qin will surely reward me heavily. Perhaps I can use this chance to obtain the true authority of a Supreme General and become the youngest Supreme General in all of Great Qin. More importantly— mm, this time I will definitely be able to break through the Ninth Layer of the Houtian Realm and advance to Level Nine.” The system promptly informed him: “Abstract Houtian Realm breakthrough.” Zhao Ji was overjoyed. “What a huge gain!” At the same time, inside Nanyang City, the flames were gradually dying down. The Zhao-Wei soldiers were pinned beneath large and small charred beams, crying out in pain for mercy. “It hurts! Spare us!” Riding calmly into the city, Zhao Ji witnessed how more than a hundred thousand Zhao-Wei soldiers had been wiped out in the great fire. Setting the city ablaze was indeed against the harmony of Heaven—but because it concerned the unification of the realm and everlasting peace, it had to be done. “Tu Sui, send the signal at once!” Tu Sui obeyed the order and immediately had the signal sounded. From the piles of debris, the Great Qin soldiers who heard the whistle all crawled up to the surface. They rushed over in force and knelt neatly before Zhao Ji, awaiting orders. All of them spoke in unison: “We pay our respects, General!” Zhao Ji immediately asked about the situation: “Those who risked their lives and rendered meritorious service in the Nanyang fire this time—were there any casualties?” A commander at Nanyang replied to Zhao Ji: “Reporting to General, after the flames erupted in Nanyang, we all hid in the fireproof chambers you had prepared in advance. Aside from two men injured in the fire, there were no casualties.” Hearing this, Zhao Ji nodded in satisfaction and said, “Very good. Go back and rest. I will not forget to reward you. Also, tell the wounded soldiers not to worry. Under my command, regardless of rank, anyone injured while carrying out a mission—I will do everything in my power to treat them and preserve their lives.” The Qin soldiers at Nanyang cupped their hands and bowed gratefully. “Many thanks, General!” Zhao Ji raised his eyes and called behind him, “Tu Sui, Zhang Han!” The two generals immediately answered, “Present, General!” Zhao Ji continued, “Keep a close watch over all the surrendered Zhao and Wei soldiers. Those in the city who were not burned are to be left alone. Anyone badly burned is to be treated—make them as comfortable as possible.” After receiving Zhao Ji’s orders, Tu Sui and Zhang Han felt deep admiration for his sense of honor. He treated his own men like brothers and would never abandon anyone. Yet toward the enemy, he showed absolutely no mercy. Their lord killed with decisive resolve. No wonder that in this great battle, no matter how richly Zhao and Wei had offered rewards, not a single man had betrayed him. Suddenly, from afar, Li Qing came galloping over on horseback with a slip of paper in hand, his voice full of joy. “General, news of victory from the front!” The moment he reached Zhao Ji, Li Qing dropped to his knees, his face shining as he said, “Li Da, acting under orders, struck the remnants of the Zhao-Wei forces at Daliang and won a complete victory, seizing all their grain supplies.” Zhao Ji was greatly pleased when he heard this. “Good. Though it is as expected, only by uprooting the Zhao-Wei forces at Daliang completely can the Battle of Nanyang truly be considered finished.” Zhao Ji then shouted, “Pass down the order to all nearby forces: no news of the Battle of Nanyang is to be leaked. The commanders have all worked hard these past few days. Let the army return to camp and rest for one day, then await this general’s further arrangements.” Confidence filled Zhao Ji’s face as he thought to himself, “As long as I seal off news of the Zhao-Wei army, I’ll be able to carry out the next step of the plan. Before that, I can also act with a little more confidence.” Zhao Ji returned to headquarters, entered his room in the military camp, and ordered the soldier guarding the door, “Without my instructions, no one is to barge in.” The soldier immediately replied, “Yes, sir!” As soon as he entered, Zhao Ji sat at his desk, opened the system screen, and ordered, “System, draw the rewards!” The system displayed: “Accepting host command. The host’s subordinates have killed a total of 98,561 people. You have obtained 24,640 experience points.” “Congratulations, Host. You have enough experience points to level up. Proceed with advancement?” Zhao Ji shouted without hesitation, “Level up!” The system screen displayed: “Accepting host command.” The moment the notification sounded, Zhao Ji’s body was immediately activated by the system for advancement. Streams of golden light wrapped around him. Surging spiritual power poured into his body, causing his cultivation to soar. The system screen congratulated him: “Congratulations, Host, on leveling up. Current level: Level Eight. Internal force upgraded, basic content upgraded, attributes upgraded.” “Congratulations, Host, on leveling up. Current level: Level Nine. Internal force upgraded.” Zhao Ji was immensely satisfied and thrilled. He said loudly, “Level Nine—I’ve finally reached it.” The system screen then displayed Zhao Ji’s status notifications: his physical level, internal force level, and basic internal cultivation technique were all at Level Nine. Martial techniques: Basic Swordsmanship cultivated to perfection—one sword strike released invisible sword qi. Mid-grade Yellow-rank martial technique Fierce Tiger Fist perfected—one punch struck out with the roar of a tiger; a single fist could gather all the body’s strength and amplify power tenfold. Yellow-rank martial technique Divine Archery mastered to perfection—arrows could be fired continuously within three hundred zhang, and ten arrows in succession carried explosive arrow qi. Weapons possessed: Star King Sword, protective armor, Ten-Stone Treasure Bow. Possessed special characteristic: Heart-Piercing. Possessed the authority of a commanding general—those beneath the rank of general would all hold him in awe. Experience required for next advancement: 1,950. After reading these notifications from the system, Zhao Ji said confidently, “I’m only a little short of the experience needed for Level Ten. After collecting the kill rewards, I wonder whether I can break through to the Xiantian Realm or not.” Then Zhao Ji gave another order to the system. “System, continue the settlement.” The system processed the request again. “Accepting host command. Continuing settlement of kill rewards. Congratulations, Host, for killing Wei Tai, young master of Wei. Reward: 300 experience points, 2,000 gold. Congratulations, Host, for killing Pang Nuan of Zhao. Reward: 800 experience points, martial technique skill. Beginning fame settlement. Congratulations, Host, for obtaining the fame of one million commoners. Reward: 100,000 upgrade points.” After reading this, Zhao Ji said, “With these extra experience points, I only need a little over 800 more to reach Level Ten. Just killing one senior general would do it. And the upgrade points have already reached 100,000. System, upgrade Pressure Point Technique and Horsemanship to perfection.” The system continued processing. “Accepting host command. Pressure Point Technique upgraded to perfection. Internal-force pressure-pointing has reached the peak level, with greater accuracy in striking acupoints. Horsemanship upgraded to perfection, reaching the state of perfect coordination between rider and horse.” Zhao Ji had now become a being of boundless strength, yet he still longed for a higher level. He thought to himself, “The Ninth Layer of the Houtian Realm is only one step away from the Xiantian Realm.” “At present, no ordinary mortal dares look down on me, but the difference between the two realms is not the same. The Houtian Realm is strong, but it still harms the body and puts one’s life at risk, whereas the Xiantian Realm doubles one’s power altogether. True qi, plus Xiantian cultivation methods—at that point, in this world, I would be something like an immortal. Even if royal power targeted me, I could still reverse the situation.” Zhao Ji sat down in a cultivation posture. The system displayed: “Upgrade successful. Remaining upgrade points: 55,000.” Zhao Ji had finished handling the rewards and upgrades with the system. He stood up and felt the abundant power surging through his body. “I didn’t expect that even after upgrading, I’d still have points left over. This time I truly made a killing. Next, I just need to wait for news of the battle to be sent back to Xianyang and receive Ying Zheng’s reward.” Zhao Ji then thought of Yuan’er and his pair of twins at home, and silently said to his wife and children, “Once the Zhao-Wei lands are settled and I reach the Xiantian Realm, I’ll be able to return home without worry and see Yuan’er and the children again.” Suddenly, a voice drifted over from afar, interrupting Zhao Ji’s train of thought. “Many thanks, Lord Xia.” Before Zhao Ji stood the military physicians, who were thanking Xia Wuju. “Physician Xia, thanks to your guidance, our methods of treating the wounded have improved more and more.” Xia Wuju replied modestly, “Not at all, not at all. It is all for Great Qin. This is simply Xia’s duty. I still need to inspect the other camps, so I must take my leave first.” Looking at Xia Wuju, Zhao Ji thought to himself, “So these past few days Xia Wuju hasn’t been sticking close to me because he’s been teaching medicine to the camp physicians. He’s really been busy.” Watching Physician Xia’s departing back, Zhao Ji immediately called out, “Lord Xia!” Zhao Ji walked over and bowed respectfully. “Lord Xia has worked tirelessly day and night. On behalf of the soldiers, I thank you, my lord.” Xia Wuju replied, “Not at all. With the general’s golden wound medicine here, I’ve only added a little effort of my own.” He stepped forward and kindly helped Zhao Ji back up, his face wearing a benevolent smile. “General Zhao leads his troops so well that the number of wounded soldiers in Great Qin is extremely low. This old man deeply admires you. Once we return to Xianyang, I will certainly praise you before the King.” Zhao Ji asked in surprise, “Lord Xia, are you leaving already?” Xia Wuju replied, “The general’s and the King’s arrangements have already fallen into place, so I have no reason to remain. I wonder whether it would be convenient, General?” Zhao Ji answered, “Please, go ahead, Lord Xia.” With Zhao Ji’s permission, Xia Wuju’s face turned troubled as he spoke of the thoughts that had weighed on his heart for a long time. “This old man has a daughter who has been missing for many years. That woman A’Fang was part of a famous tale. Her familiar name is A’Fang.” Just as Zhao Ji had thought. “I always thought that was only a legend. I never expected it to be true.” Xia Wuju’s face now turned hopeful as he asked, “General Zhao, may I ask the name of your elder?” Zhao Ji scratched his head awkwardly. “I’m afraid I’ll disappoint you, Lord Xia. My mother’s name was Zhao Dong’er, so I am not your grandson.” Xia Wuju was somewhat disappointed by this. Zhao Ji comforted him at once. “It’s hard to avoid lookalikes in this world. But Lord Xia, don’t lose heart. Zhao Ji’s face is almost the same as A’Fang’s. I wonder whether this old man might meet her just once?” Zhao Ji suddenly turned away, his voice becoming sorrowful. “My mother passed away a year ago.” Startled, Xia Wuju asked, “Passed away?” Zhao Ji continued, “It was precisely because my mother died that I enlisted in the army without anything holding me back.” Seeing the lingering shock on Xia Wuju’s face, he consoled him. “General, please restrain your grief. This old man has asked something he should not have.” Zhao Ji replied, “It’s alright. Lord Xia asked only because he misses his daughter. I understand.” Xia Wuju cupped his hands gratefully and said to Zhao Ji, “In any case, many thanks to General Zhao for resolving the doubts in this old man’s heart. I take my leave.” Zhao Ji replied, “It was only a small matter, Lord Xia. There is no need to thank me.” As Xia Wuju turned to leave, his bearing became dejected and sorrowful. “A’Fang, A’Fang, I thought I had found you this time. In the end, where are you?” “Could Zhao Ji truly not be my grandson? Why do I feel such a sense of closeness toward him? Could it really just be coincidence?” But Xia Wuju quickly rallied himself and said decisively, “No. Even if there is only a sliver of hope, I must not give up.” He turned and looked at Zhao Ji’s departing figure, his face extremely serious as he said with anticipation, “In a few days, I’ll set out for Li Family Village and see for myself whether you are truly my grandson—whether you are A’Fang’s son.” Zhao Ji walked to the front of all the Great Qin soldiers and declared in a ringing voice, “Soldiers, hear the report on the Battle of Nanyang—Great Qin has won a complete victory!” The moment they heard it, all the soldiers erupted in excitement and shouted in unison, “Great Qin!” Zhao Ji raised a hand to signal them to stop, and the soldiers immediately fell silent. The atmosphere became solemn and still. Zhao Ji continued, recounting the achievements of the Battle of Nanyang. “In this battle, our army lost 2,685 dead and 3,100 wounded. Nine out of ten men emerged safe and sound. We annihilated 100,000 enemy troops and captured 80,000 Zhao-Wei soldiers alive. Since the founding of Great Qin, this is truly a victory rarely seen in all ages.” The moment Zhao Ji finished speaking, the soldiers below erupted into joyous cheers. They were beyond grateful. One soldier exclaimed happily, “I actually got to take part in such a once-in-a-lifetime battle!” The man beside him chimed in, “With a victory like this, even if I retire and return home in the future, it’ll be enough to make me proud for the rest of my life.” Some were so overjoyed they were moved to tears. Looking at the soldiers below, Zhao Ji continued, “Therefore, this general has decided to reward the entire army, and at the same time fulfill the promise I made to you at the beginning.” Raising both hands, Zhao Ji loudly proclaimed to the whole army regarding the Battle of Nanyang, “Whether old troops of Kongcheng or newly enlisted surrendered soldiers, all of you have rendered great merit for Great Qin and shall be rewarded equally. All elite Qin soldiers and officers will be raised one rank in nobility.” General Tu Sui, General Zhang Han, and the other commanders, upon hearing this, laughed joyfully and thanked Zhao Ji for the reward. As for the common soldiers, Zhao Ji continued, “All surrendered soldiers who enlisted shall have their slave status removed and truly become soldiers of Great Qin. You will enjoy all the privileges of our Great Qin, and from now on may earn higher rank year after year through killing enemies.” Upon hearing this, the surrendered soldiers all teared up and said emotionally, “I… I’ve been freed from slave status. I’m truly a soldier of Great Qin now. General Zhao didn’t lie to us.” The Qin soldiers were also happy for them. The soldiers began cheering again. “General Zhao! General Zhao! General Zhao!” Zhao Ji closed his eyes in satisfaction and savored the atmosphere of victory. Amid the crowd’s cries of admiration, he laughed silently to himself. “Are they cheering for me, Zhao Ji? The gains from this battle are enormous—nothing surpasses the hearts of the army and one’s reputation.” Zhao Ji turned and patted the shoulder of a nearby officer. “Prepare mutton for the troops and pass down this general’s order: today we eat meat; when the enemy lands are fully pacified, we’ll reward the army with wine.” That officer immediately accepted the order. Zhao Ji then mounted his warhorse and, sword in hand, led the army from the front. “The Han territory has already been rewarded. Next, I only need to wait for the influence and recognition granted to me by the King of Qin, and for the Qin cavalry to sweep through Zhao. I, Zhao Ji, am destined to be the vanguard.” At the same time, in the main hall of Xianyang, the ministers were taking turns reporting to the King of Qin. “Your Majesty, Zhao and Wei have already mobilized, but we still have not been able to dispatch the main army in time. What should be done about Wei City?” Another also added, “Han territory is in critical danger. We beg Your Majesty to decide quickly.” The King of Great Qin had only a faint trace of concern on his face as he reassured the ministers. “My lords need not worry. Han territory is not in danger.” Seated firmly on his throne, the King continued, “Earlier, I already received secret reports from Han territory: the Zhao-Wei army has already been crushed by Zhao Ji.” “Zhao Gao, read the memorial.” Zhao Gao immediately replied, “Yes.” The ministers below were shocked and astonished. “Wasn’t Zhao Ji supposed to be dead?” Paying them no mind, Zhao Gao began to read the memorial. “The 180,000 allied Zhao-Wei troops attacked Nanyang City. Commander Zhao Ji devised a plan, lured the enemy into the city, and set it ablaze. Of the tens of thousands of Zhao-Wei troops who entered the city, nearly all perished. In addition, 80,000 enemy troops were taken alive. Great Qin suffered fewer than 2,000 dead and fewer than 3,000 wounded, while the common people of Nanyang all remained safe and sound. Wei general Wei Tai was shot to death by Commander Zhao Ji. Zhao general Pang Nuan was also beheaded by Commander Zhao Ji.” After hearing this, the ministers below all rejoiced and began discussing noisily among themselves. “Burning an empty city in exchange for 100,000 Zhao-Wei troops—what a brilliant plan!” “The deaths of the Zhao-Wei generals truly show Heaven is blessing Great Qin!” “Since the founding of Great Qin, and even among all the states under Heaven until now, which country has ever won such a great victory with such a vast disparity in casualties?” “But what exactly happened? Even if Zhao Ji wasn’t dead, when did he dispatch troops?” Only Li Si, after hearing the memorial, turned pale with shock, scarcely able to believe his ears. His expression became dark and thoughtful. “Zhao Ji isn’t dead, which means the assassination plot has been exposed. If that’s the case, then the hatred between him and me is now utterly irreconcilable.” At that moment, the King of Qin laughed loudly. “My lords, by this point, there is no need for me to conceal the truth any longer. From Zhao Ji being gravely wounded in an assassination attempt to the fake reinforcement army from Yongcheng, all of it was a game of chess arranged by Zhao Ji and me, to lure Zhao and Wei into raising troops. And Zhao Ji has indeed not disappointed me—nor has he disappointed Great Qin.” “This time, Zhao Ji not only secured order in Han territory and defeated 180,000 Zhao-Wei troops, he also killed Wei Tai and Pang Nuan, completely shaking the two states of Zhao and Wei. Han territory has been stabilized. Zhao and Wei have suffered grievous losses to their vital strength. Great Qin now has a famed commanding general—our chance to seize all under Heaven has come far sooner than expected.” The King of Qin slammed his hand down on the map table, and the small markers representing Zhao and Wei snapped apart. He continued, “Prepare for war immediately. Within two months, I want Great Qin’s forces to leave Hangu Pass and smash through the border cities of Zhao State.” The ministers immediately bowed their heads respectfully and said in unison, “Your Majesty is wise and mighty. We swear to follow Your Majesty unto death and unify all under Heaven for Great Qin.” Meng Yi, Meng Wu’s second son, immediately stepped forward and said to the King, “Your Majesty, in this battle in Han territory, Zhao Ji has rendered a feat of merit without equal. I believe he must be richly rewarded.” Meng Yi’s proposal made Li Si somewhat uneasy. The King of Great Qin gave a hearty laugh and said, “Minister Meng is absolutely right.” Then the King proclaimed his decree: “Reward Zhao Ji with 3,000 gold, 3,000 bolts of cloth, 500 maidservants, 1,000 slaves, and an additional 2,500 troops. Yongcheng and his hometown, Li Family Village, are also to be enfeoffed as his fief. In addition, Zhao Ji’s noble rank shall be raised by two grades; he is promoted to Upper General and elevated to commander of a full army. From today onward, military affairs in Han territory need no longer be reported to the Yongcheng command camp—all matters shall be managed independently.” The other ministers all voiced their agreement as well: “Your Majesty is wise and resourceful, and with a fierce general like Zhao Ji, the territory of our Great Qin will soon expand further.” Another minister chimed in: “Great Qin is truly fortunate to have Zhao Ji.” Only Li Si still stood in the back, face dark with resentment, lost in thought. Meng Yi walked over, leaned close to Li Si’s ear, and said, “Lord Commandant, why do you seem so dispirited?” Startled, Li Si stammered, “Meng... Meng Yi.” Not giving him a chance to continue, Meng Yi smiled and went on, “Let me guess— are you unhappy because His Majesty granted your fief to Zhao Ji? Didn’t His Majesty say he would grant you another fief? What is there to feel troubled about?” Li Si immediately denied it: “I have no dissatisfaction with His Majesty.” Meng Yi replied, “Of course you’re dissatisfied—because you lost your fief, and from now on it’ll be much harder for you to make trouble for Madam Zhao. And besides, Zhao Ji’s promotion this time also makes you unhappy, doesn’t it?” Li Si had been hit right where it hurt. Furious, he was left speechless and unable to retort. Seeing him like that, Meng Yi turned and laughed smugly. “I was just joking, Lord Commandant. Don’t take it to heart.” Li Si burned with anger inside. “Meng Yi’s insolence must be because Meng Wu is backing him.” Watching Meng Yi’s self-satisfied figure walk away, Li Si frowned and thought, “But he’s not wrong. If Zhao Ji is made Upper General, then I won’t be able to control Li Yuan’er anymore either. And with the Meng family supporting him, it’ll be harder than climbing to the heavens to move against Zhao Ji in court in the future.” Court had already adjourned. At this moment, in the inner palace, a voice announced: “Your Majesty, Imperial Physician Xia has returned.” The King of Qin, Qin Shi Huang, had been alone in contemplation, gazing at a painting, when he ordered that Xia Wuju be admitted. As soon as Xia Wuju arrived, he respectfully bowed. “This old subject pays his respects to Your Majesty.” The King of Qin immediately reached out to help Xia Wuju up. “Father-in-law, there are only the two of us here, so there is no need for such formality. You’ve worked hard on this trip.” The two of them looked together at the painting on the wall. Xia Wuju said, “To give my all for Your Majesty, this old subject does not fear hardship. After all these years, does Your Majesty still long for A Fang?” The King of Qin’s voice grew slightly heavy. “How could true feelings ever be forgotten? Back then, I only hate that I had not yet truly secured royal power, and so caused her to avoid me for so many years. One day, when I unite all under Heaven, I will surely find her. At that time, nothing will be able to separate us again.” Thinking back on what had happened, Xia Wuju comforted the King. “You cannot blame her. A Fang understood, and that is why she left.” Looking at the King’s back, at the man who loved his daughter so deeply, Xia Wuju thought to himself, “Back then, Lao Ai, Zhao Ji, Lü Buwei, the old aristocratic clans—countless people relied on royal power, countless people obstructed them. That was also what gave rise to his longing for power. But the road to power is full of hardship and bitterness. And yet, his feelings for A Fang have remained unchanged from beginning to end. This is the only driving force on the path he walks. And because of this love, there is the present King of Qin, and the present Great Qin.” While lost in thought, Xia Wuju heard the King of Qin ask, “By the way, on your trip to Han territory this time, what impression did Zhao Ji leave on you? What kind of person is he?” Xia Wuju replied, “General Zhao is a true talent. Though he is young, he already carries the bearing of a great general. He acts cleanly and decisively, and when it comes to killing, he is firm and resolute. He is a rare hero indeed.” At the mention of Zhao Ji, Xia Wuju lowered his head and thought, “There is even a trace of Your Majesty and A Fang in him.” But those words could not be said carelessly. Moreover, his mother’s name was Zhao Dong’er, and that matter had not yet been verified. Hearing Xia Wuju’s assessment of Zhao Ji, the King of Qin said, “Sure enough, he is much like I imagined. After this campaign to destroy Zhao, I must summon him back to the capital and meet him once. Sometimes I think that if Dong’er and I had a child, perhaps he would be just like him.” When Xia Wuju heard the King of Qin mention the name Dong’er, he was so startled that he blurted out, “Dong’er?” The King of Qin smiled and said, “Father-in-law, did you not know? Dong’er is the private pet name that A Fang and I used for each other.” Xia Wuju’s face turned pale, and he thought inwardly, “Dong’er... was my guess correct? Then my A Fang...” The King of Qin frowned and asked, “What is it?” Xia Wuju lowered his head and answered, “Ah, it is nothing, this old subject... I was simply surprised to suddenly learn that A Fang had another name. Your Majesty, I hurried back to the capital to pay my respects because there is another matter I wished to speak of. This old subject, while caring for General Zhao in Han territory, learned that the general’s wife has given birth. I wish to contribute what little strength I can and request leave to go to Li Family Village to help them recover their health.” The King of Qin smiled and said, “So that is the matter. Since you are willing, then take Zhao Ji’s reward with you as well.” Xia Wuju cupped his hands. “Yes. Then this old subject shall take his leave first.” On the way back, Xia Wuju walked while thinking, “Dong’er is A Fang. A Fang is Dong’er—my daughter. Did you really leave your old father and the man you loved just like that? No—unless I personally verify it, I absolutely refuse to believe it. And His Majesty must never learn of this. If His Majesty learns that you are dead, then what would remain to support him as the pillar of Great Qin? The world would surely fall into chaos.” At the same time, at the Zhao residence in Li Family Village, a convoy of carriages appeared, bringing a great quantity of gold, silver, and treasures. The people standing at a distance clicked their tongues in amazement. “What joyous news, joyous news indeed! General Zhao Ji has been promoted to Upper General!” Someone beside them said with a touch of envy, “Are all those His Majesty’s rewards? What honor! Heaven truly has eyes, bringing such good fortune to Yuan’er.” Inside the room, after taking Yuan’er’s pulse, Xia Wuju said, “Madam’s health is not in any serious danger. It is only that her emotions are somewhat unstable.” Meng Tian at once replied, “Lord Xia’s medical skill is unmatched. Yuan’er worries about Zhao Ji all day long, and before this she was even harassed by that old bastard Li Si. Naturally her spirit has been harmed. But that brat Zhao Ji has won His Majesty’s favor. Step by step, he has risen until now he is already an Upper General. Even Li Family Village has become his personal fief. Presumably Yuan’er can finally feel a little more at ease.” Yuan’er took the jade pendant and gazed at it gently. “Brother Ji really did it. Ji’er, Xi’er, our family will soon be reunited.” Looking at the jade pendant in Li Yuan’er’s hand, Xia Wuju was inwardly shocked. “That jade pendant...” He immediately asked, “Madam Zhao, that jade pendant of yours is exquisitely crafted. May I know where it came from? An old friend of mine also had a jade pendant quite similar to it.” Li Yuan’er’s eyes widened in surprise. “Actually, this jade pendant is a keepsake left behind by my mother-in-law. I heard it was also the love token my parents-in-law exchanged back then. My mother-in-law, even until the moment she died, still remembered him. But for many years, there was no word from him at all. If my lord has seen this jade pendant before, then perhaps you might be able to help my husband and his father reunite.” Xia Wuju looked at the jade pendant, his eyes full of sorrow. “So my guess was right after all. A Fang... right now, I truly wish all of this were wrong.” Seeing Xia Wuju’s expression, Meng Tian immediately began to speculate. “That jade pendant really is something important to His Majesty. So Zhao Ji truly is the son of His Majesty and A Fang. This matter absolutely cannot be spoken aloud.” Meng Tian then reached out, placed a hand on Xia Wuju’s shoulder, and said, “Lord Xia, look carefully. There are many jade pendants in this world that look similar.” Xia Wuju lowered his eyes and replied, “At first glance, it does seem very similar. But the more closely one looks, the less alike they seem. I am afraid this old man cannot help Madam Zhao.” Li Yuan’er smiled and said, “It’s all right. In this vast sea of people, finding someone who vanished is no easy matter. Lord Xia, you may simply call me Yuan’er. Please don’t call me Madam Zhao. And besides, you are an elder. I ought to call you Grandpa.” Xia Wuju was immediately moved. “May I really?” Li Yuan’er nodded. “Of course, Grandpa.” Then she pushed her two children forward toward Xia Wuju. Xia Wuju held the two children in his arms, his face full of joy, while sighing inwardly with regret. “A Fang, forgive your father for coming too late and not seeing you one last time. I cannot even acknowledge kinship with Zhao Ji now. But to hear your daughter-in-law call me Grandpa, to see the descendants of your son—even if I died now, I would have no regrets.” After the three of them left, father and son Meng Wu and Meng Tian brought Xia Wuju to visit his daughter’s grave. Xia Wuju laid his hand on the gravestone, his face filled with grief. “A Fang, Father has come to see you.” Standing at a distance, Meng Tian asked his father in confusion, “Father, is Zhao Ji really His Majesty’s son? This is a good thing, so why hide it? Besides, if Zhao Ji acknowledges his ancestry, it would surely bring many benefits to our Meng family as well.” Meng Wu immediately scolded him. “You foolish boy, keep your voice down. The problem is that Zhao Ji is the son of Xia Yufang. Back then, when His Majesty was a hostage in Zhao and suffered humiliation, only the Xia family’s young daughter, A Fang, cared for him attentively. The two of them were childhood sweethearts and had already resolved to spend their lives together. Later, when His Majesty returned to Great Qin, he originally wished to take A Fang as his wife. Who could have expected Lü Buwei and those others to obstruct it so overbearingly, claiming that A Fang was of humble birth? They even used the struggle for the throne as an excuse. Later, in order to allow His Majesty to stabilize his realm, A Fang left without hesitation. From the moment A Fang departed, His Majesty seemed to go mad, climbing to the summit of power—controlling Zhao Ji, killing Lao Ai, reforming through Shang Gong, eliminating the old aristocratic clans, and seizing power from Lü Buwei. It can be said that at least half of His Majesty’s ambition today comes from his attachment to A Fang. But if he were to learn now that A Fang is dead, then what would become of our Great Qin and the great enterprise of unifying all under Heaven?” Meng Tian nodded in realization. “No wonder His Majesty still has not established a queen after all these years. So it is because his love runs that deep. But paper cannot wrap fire forever.” Meng Wu raised his head to the sky and said, “Fortunately, there is still Zhao Ji and Zhao Ji’s two children. Once the realm is stable, we can inform him little by little. Perhaps for the sake of his children, His Majesty will still be able to keep his reason.” Meng Tian stroked his chin and added, “And with the feelings His Majesty has for A Fang, together with Zhao Ji’s current performance, once the truth comes to light in the future, His Majesty may even establish him as crown prince. Li Si put all his effort into currying favor with Prince Fusu, yet ended up overlooking the true eldest legitimate son—what a huge loss.” Meng Wu rubbed his son’s head and laughed. “As expected of my son—clever indeed. We originally thought our Meng family, as great ministers, was merely supporting a powerful frontier general. But now it seems we are standing on the side of the future master of all under Heaven. In the future, this will be a blessing for Great Qin, and also a blessing for our Meng family.” On a fine evening, at Jinyang City, at the meeting point of the Three Jin, a convoy of carriages carrying a large amount of grain appeared. The guard on the city wall saw it and immediately reported, “General, there is a group of men and horses ahead.” The man beside him folded his arms and replied with a smile, “What are you panicking for? Isn’t that the banner and armor of our Zhao troops? General Pang went south to Nanyang—most likely this is just a grain transport.” One of the mounted men below rode forward and shouted toward the city gate, “Brother on the wall, trouble you to open the gate. We’ve come under the general’s orders to distribute provisions.” A hanging basket was lowered on ropes. The man above said, “Fine. Put your copy of the military order into the basket. After I inspect it, I’ll open the gate.” When the basket was pulled back up, the defending general took out the command token inside. After examining it carefully, he nodded. “The token is genuine. Open the city gate.” The gate slowly opened. Seeing all the men and horses outside, the leader at the front cupped his hands in salute. “Brothers, you’ve worked hard. We still have to trouble you after entering the city, or Upper General Lian Po will blame us. I wonder how the fighting in Nanyang is going now? When will General Pang Nuan return in triumph?” The expression of Tu Wei, who was leading the men outside the city, darkened. He gave a sinister smile. “Hahaha, you want to know that badly? Then lower your head, and this general will tell you.” The moment he finished speaking, his blade swept forward. Blood immediately sprayed from the throat of the man in front of him. He raised his sword and shouted, “By General Zhao’s command: when the army enters the city, no civilians are to be harmed. Secure the gate at once. Those who surrender will not be killed. Those who refuse to surrender—kill without mercy!” As soon as he spoke, the troops outside the city surged in. Several soldiers inside the city cried out in horror, “Qin soldiers! Qin soldiers have arrived!” The man beside them stared blankly. “What happened? How could Qin soldiers enter the city?” From outside came wave after wave of shouts in unison: “Surrender and you live! Refuse and you die!” The two sides clashed, and the firelight cast swaying shadows against the walls. Inside their homes, the people huddled together in fear. Several soldiers realized the situation was hopeless and quickly raised their hands in surrender. “I surrender! I surrender! Don’t kill me! Spare me!” The soldiers of Zhao were crushed just like that. Qin troops poured in and slaughtered their way forward, finally seizing the city. Zhao Ji rode in on horseback, looked around, and assessed the situation inwardly. “Jinyang fell too easily. Fifty li behind it lies Handan.” Tu Wei walked up to Zhao Ji’s horse and cupped his hands in report. “General, the entire area around Jinyang’s city gate is now under our control. Most of Zhao’s soldiers and officers have surrendered. Only a small number stubbornly resisted, but they have already been dealt with.” Zhao Ji smiled and said, “Block all news. Do not allow any word of the city’s fall to leak out. That way, we can keep using the same method, relying on these Zhao armors to approach Handan without anyone the wiser.” “Yes, sir.” A captured Zhao general, bound in ropes, glared at Zhao Ji and shouted bitterly, “Qin dog, you are truly despicable! But don’t think yourself so formidable. When General Pang returns victorious from Nanyang, he will cut off the heads of every last one of you!” Tu Wei laughed mockingly. “Hahaha, you idiot—have you not thought about where the Zhao armor we’re wearing came from? Let me tell you: Pang Nuan was long since killed by General Zhao. Your 100,000 Zhao troops also died at Nanyang. Do you expect them to come back as ghosts to reinforce you?” Hearing this, the man’s face changed dramatically. “What?” Tu Wei turned to Zhao Ji and cupped his hands. “General, how should we deal with Zhao’s soldiers and officers? Should we absorb them into our ranks, as we did with Han?” The Zhao general immediately shouted in fury, “Qin dog! We would rather die than surrender to you! Don’t even dream that our Zhao will bow at your feet!” Zhao Ji curled his lips in a smile. “Hahaha, quite spirited—worthy of this general’s admiration. In that case, I’ll grant your wish. Those who do not surrender shall be killed.” As soon as he finished speaking, several swords from the surrounding soldiers pierced through the Zhao general’s body. Zhao Ji turned and walked away, thinking inwardly, “Han has already been destroyed by Great Qin, so its officers and soldiers can be peacefully incorporated. But Zhao’s soldiers still have a state to support them. If they do not surrender, they absolutely cannot be kept alive.” He then asked the system, “This battle was won so easily. I wonder what the gains were.” The system began calculating the reward for enemy kills. A notice appeared on the system screen. “Acknowledged, Host’s command. In this battle, the forces under the Host’s command killed 5,235 enemies and obtained 1,308 experience points. Level-up available. Experience is full. Would you like to raise your level?” Zhao Ji nodded. “Level up.” The instant he spoke, spiritual energy surged throughout his entire body, and both his inner force and physical strength increased. “Level 10 Acquired Realm Peak.” At that moment, the system issued a new notification. “Character: Zhao Ji. Level 10 Acquired Realm. Physical Strength: 1000. Inner Force: 1000. Cultivation Technique: Basic Internal Skill, Level 10. Martial Skill Training: Basic Swordsmanship, perfected; with one slash, invisible sword qi is released. Mid-Gold Rank Martial Skill, perfected: Fierce Tiger Fist; each punch carries the roar of a tiger, and one strike can gather ten times the full-body power into an explosive blow. Mysterious Rank perfected skill: Vast Divine Archery; fully comprehended—three hundred million illusory arrows, ten arrows fired in succession including explosive arrows. Weapons: Overlord’s refined-steel sword-halberd, ten-stone bow. Defensive armor equipped. Treasure: Conscience Measure. Trait: Commanding Authority of the Chief General. All subordinate generals hold deep awe and respect. Authority value: 9560.” Holding the authority token in his hand, he felt delighted inside. “My army is now truly close to a state where no one can stop us. Zhao really is on the verge of exhaustion.” A voice sounded from behind him. “My lord, your subordinate has carried out your command. All Zhao troops who refused to surrender have been executed. As for the remaining surrendered troops, how should they be handled? Our army is now stationed at the junction of the Three Jin. For the next campaign, should we request instructions from Xianyang?” Zhao Ji turned and replied, “Send ten thousand officers and soldiers to escort the surrendered Zhao troops back to Qin. Anyone who causes trouble on the road—kill them at once. Let the army rest and reorganize briefly. In a few days, we march on Zhao’s Anyang City. There is no need to seek instructions from Xianyang.” Tu Wei immediately said, “My lord, forgive this subordinate for speaking bluntly. To attack Anyang is to push deep into Zhao’s heartland. If we do not seek instructions from Xianyang, then we will be a lone force, isolated and unsupported. If—if our army should be defeated, then His Majesty will have no way to quickly send troops to aid us.” Zhao Ji frowned. “Do you think I am being rash and arrogantly overconfident?” Tu Wei lowered his head. “This subordinate would not dare.” Zhao Ji smiled and said, “Relax. I would never risk the lives of Great Qin’s soldiers recklessly. This time, our army took the city very quickly. All secret letters and military defense maps in Jinyang’s command room must be destroyed and concealed. At this moment, a surprise attack on Zhao is our best path to victory. Besides, to capture bandits, one must first capture their king. Zhao is the strongest of the Three Jin, so naturally it must be eliminated first.” He placed a hand on Zhao’s map and thought smugly to himself, “The First Emperor of all ages— would you really let slip the chance to destroy a great enemy? So if I know this, then surely you know it as well.” Early the next morning, the guard atop the city wall saw a Zhao soldier galloping away in flight. The Zhao soldier looked at the corpses strewn everywhere around him, his face filled with panic. The gate guard immediately said, “Master, are you really letting him escape to report back to Handan like this?” Zhao Ji glanced behind him and said with a smile, “That’s right. When panic makes men lose their way and chaos destroys all order, the fear created in the enemy is precisely the key to victory. What I want now is complete turmoil in their court. If we seize this chance and press the army forward to besiege the city, success is certain.” He then shouted his orders to the whole army. “Remove the disguises and put on Great Qin armor. Leave ten thousand men to garrison Anyang City. The remaining one hundred thousand troops are to follow this general at once to attack Handan. No need to reorganize or refit.” At this time in Handan, inside Longtai Palace, the King of Zhao turned pale in fright upon hearing the report. “What? Pang Nuan is dead in battle? Jinyang and Anyang have both fallen one after another? All one hundred thousand of our Zhao-Wei allied troops have been wiped out?” The soldier delivering the report burst into tears. “Your Majesty, Zhao Ji was too cunning. We were all deceived. The Qin army is now only a dozen li away and will soon reach Handan.” The King of Zhao shouted, “That old fool Pang Nuan was utterly useless and has dragged me into such a trap!” As he spoke, he became so enraged that he coughed up blood. The old minister standing behind him grew anxious at once. “Your Majesty, please take care of your health.” The king turned to him in panic. “Chancellor, what should we do now? The Qin troops are pressing in. If Handan falls, Great Zhao is finished.” The Chancellor of Zhao supported him and comforted him. “Your Majesty, do not panic. We still have fifty thousand elite troops in Handan. We will certainly keep Your Majesty safe.” Another minister also nodded frantically. “That’s right. We still have fifty thousand soldiers in Handan. It’s not as if the city can be defeated so easily. As long as we hold out for a few days and order General Lian Po to hurry back and reinforce the city, the Qin army will surely withdraw.” A voice suddenly rang out in the middle of the hall. “That plan cannot be used!” Zhao Ba, the Crown Prince of Zhao and Lord Chunping, stepped forward in the hall and cupped his hands. “Your Majesty, General Lian Po is guarding the frontier and pinning down Wang Jian. If we order him to lead his army back to Handan at once, Wang Jian will seize the opportunity to invade.” “Then what are we supposed to do?” “In your servant’s opinion, it would be better to order General Li Mu to return and reinforce us. Even if Handan falls, Zhao’s lands can still be kept safe.” Hearing this, the King of Zhao pointed straight at Zhao Ba and cursed, “Silence! Zhao Ba, what are you plotting? Is my safety worth less than a few border cities? The one who can return to Handan the fastest is Lian Po. If Li Mu comes back instead, do you think I’ll still be alive by then?” “Zhao Ba, do you want me dead so badly? Are you still coveting this throne?” Zhao Ba lowered his head at once. “I would not dare. I harbor no such thoughts.” The King of Zhao snorted. “It had better be so.” He waved his hand and shouted, “My decision is final. Send orders at once for Lian Po to lead his troops back to Handan and rescue me. Zhao Ba, since you have always been loyal to the state, I now appoint you general, commander of the fifty thousand troops defending the outer city. If the city falls, bring me your head.” Zhao Ba answered helplessly, “This subject obeys.” After saying that, the King of Zhao turned around. “All of you, withdraw.” As the two old ministers were leaving, they whispered to each other. One sighed, “His Majesty is muddle-headed. Lord Chunping’s plan was clearly the best course, yet he listened to Guo Kai’s slander instead.” The other replied, “With the enemy army pressing down amid such chaos, His Majesty’s decision is understandable. But if General Lian Po withdraws, I fear the border cities of Great Zhao will soon be trampled by Qin cavalry.” The minister beside him added, “To ignore the greater situation like this... if Lord Chunping had succeeded to the throne from the start, Great Zhao would never have ended up in this state.” The man opposite him paled in fright. “Shh, lower your voice!” After Zhao Ba arrived at the city outskirts to take command, a soldier on the wall reported to him on the day both sides faced off. “Reporting to Lord Chunping, the fifty thousand Zhao troops inside the city are ready for battle.” Zhao Ba nodded. “Mm.” Standing atop the gate tower and looking into the distance at the tens of thousands of Qin troops, he thought to himself, The life or death of Great Zhao depends on this battle. I only hope I can hold the city until General Lian Po returns. Drawing his sword from its scabbard, Zhao Ba shouted, “Soldiers of Great Zhao! Violent Qin is cruel and savage. In the Battle of Changping, Lord Wu’an set a trap and slaughtered four hundred thousand of our kin. And now they come again, seeking to destroy Great Zhao. Do you dare fight to the death for Great Zhao, for all the people in this city?” All the Zhao soldiers raised their swords and roared in unison, “Kill violent Qin! Kill violent Qin!” Lord Chunping shouted loudly, “With one heart, soldiers of Zhao, defend the city and wait for General Lian Po’s reinforcements. Then we will kill the Qin generals!” All the Zhao soldiers shouted together, “Avenge our hatred! Avenge our hatred! We will avenge our hatred!” At that moment, Zhao Ji was already riding his warhorse with Zhang Han and Tu Sui, pressing close to the city of Zhao. Seeing that only fifty thousand soldiers had come out to meet them, Zhao Ji could not help but sneer. “Only fifty thousand troops? And they still dare face me? The cavalry of Great Qin still carries a sky-piercing aura. Who is the commander leading them?” General Tu Sui quickly answered, “Reporting to General Zhao, the man leading the troops over there is the Crown Prince of Zhao, Lord Chunping.” Hearing this, Zhao Ji grew even more confident. “No wonder Zhao is only capable of this much.” As they drew closer to the city, Zhao Ji became even more excited. While advancing, he asked, “Tu Sui, faced with this sort of provocation, where are the elite troops of Great Qin?” The elite soldiers marching behind him were already burning with fighting spirit, ready for battle. They had now arrived beneath the Zhao city commanded by Lord Chunping. Zhao Ji forcefully drew his sword and pointed it straight at the city as he advanced. He shouted, “Soldiers! For many years the realm has been wracked by war, and the common people have suffered, all because Handan believed Great Qin had already been brought low. Today our army will wipe out Zhao completely.” Zhao Ji continued to rouse the courage of Qin’s soldiers. “Break Handan, raise the campaign to destroy Zhao, and from here begin Great Qin’s unification of the world.” “General Zhao Ji, we will fight alongside the soldiers of Great Qin to destroy Zhao and begin a new age of prosperity for the emperor of Great Qin!” After hearing this, the soldiers of Great Qin all surged forward with blazing fervor, swords in hand, charging straight at the city walls. The great gate thundered, and Zhao Ji, sword in hand atop his warhorse, led the assault as the army pushed into the attack on Zhao’s city. As they neared, General Tu Sui ordered the troops to form defensive positions at once. The soldiers of Great Qin lined up, raised their bows, and set their shields in place, preparing to attack into the city. But this defensive formation looked rather strange. Compared with ordinary formations, it left the Zhao officers stunned and suspicious. “What is this? Why are the archers in front? What on earth are they doing? We’ve never seen a formation like this before.” Lord Chunping had no time to think deeply. He brushed it off and did not concern himself with the formation any further. Maybe they were only trying to frighten them. As long as they were not allowed to get close, that would be enough. So Lord Chunping ordered the archers to fire downward. Zhao Ji also issued orders to his troops. “At one hundred zhang, raise bows. Archers, prepare. Catapults, take your positions and stand by.” Zhao Ji was extremely confident in his advantage. “Did they think a few childish toys like that could trouble the soldiers of Great Qin?” “All soldiers of Great Qin, listen well. Let little Zhao learn what true archery really is.” With that, the soldiers of Great Qin began drawing their bows and firing toward Lord Chunping. Thousands of arrows shot toward the city wall in a shrill storm. Toward the place where Lord Chunping stood, there came not only sharp arrows but hundreds of heavy stones as well. Lord Chunping froze in place in shock. His entire group cried out in terror and scattered in all directions. As he fled for his life, Lord Chunping thought, So this is Great Qin’s archers and catapults? At such a distance, and yet the power is this great... truly terrifying. By the time they arrived, Zhao Ji had long since ridden away on Blood Tiger. All that remained were the corpses of the nomads on the ground, marked with huge claw wounds.
