Since when have the people of our northern border had the strength to fight back against the nomads like this?” Supreme General Li Mu observed the state of the corpses for a while, then said grimly, “No. The fatal wounds on these nomads were inflicted by military weapons. There are also claw marks from a ferocious beast. This was absolutely not done by ordinary villagers. Besides, on the way here we saw no corpses of civilians at all. This is highly suspicious.” At that moment, a villager stepped out from behind a large rock and looked at Li Mu. “Are you General Li Mu?” The officer beside Li Mu immediately shouted, “Who are you?” The villager replied, “I am from this village. About two hours ago, the nomads suddenly attacked. Fortunately, a young general arrived in time and saved us. He also helped us find a temporary safe place. That young general asked me to invite General Li Mu to come alone.” After hearing this, a trace of surprise appeared on Li Mu’s face. He thought to himself: One man killing an entire group of nomads—how was that possible? Then he asked the villager, “Where is he now? Quickly take me to him.” Li Mu and the officer at his side were led by the villager to where Zhao Ji and Blood Tiger were waiting. The moment he saw Li Mu’s figure, Zhao Ji spoke first. “Supreme General, I’ve been waiting for you for quite a while.” Li Mu, still seated on horseback, looked at Zhao Ji, who was leisurely wiping the large spear in his hand while Blood Tiger lay beside him dozing. He rode closer and asked, “You are from Qin?” Zhao Ji replied, “That’s right. I am Zhao Ji, a general of Qin. I have long heard of General Li’s great name. Would you be willing to dismount and talk?” Li Mu immediately got off his horse. Looking at the young general before him, he thought, So this is Zhao Ji—the man who successively killed Pang Nuan and Lian Po? No wonder he could single-handedly deal with a band of nomads. I just didn’t expect him to be so young. And he can even control a tiger. Li Mu said to Zhao Ji, “General, why are you here? In any case, I should thank you for saving the people of my northern border from danger.” Zhao Ji planted his spear on the ground and replied, “The nomads are guilty. As a descendant of Yan and Huang, how could I stand by and watch my own people be bullied and slaughtered? Since we are of one people, and the foreign tribes are at fault, General Li need not thank me.” As Zhao Ji spoke, Li Mu’s mind filled with the scornful words of Zhao’s court officials: “A lowborn man dares call himself Supreme General? He is nothing more than a watchdog for Great Zhao. Those vulgar men at your side dare call themselves Zhao people too? Shameless.” Thinking of those arrogant officials, Li Mu inwardly praised Zhao Ji. It was precisely because they were descendants of Yan and Huang that he had stationed himself at Dai and fought bravely to kill the enemy, yet not a single person in the entire court understood him. This young general of Qin was more clear-sighted than them all. Li Mu said to Zhao Ji, “Well said—one people of Yan and Huang, and the foreign tribes are at fault. I never imagined that the one who understood me after all these years would be a man from violent Qin.” Li Mu stepped before Zhao Ji and said sternly, “Enough small talk. You lured me here alone—what is it you want? Do you intend to fight me to the death here to solve Wang Jian and Huan Yi’s problem?” Hearing Li Mu’s words, Zhao Ji suddenly burst into laughter. “Underhanded assassination tactics like that are something only Guo Kai would do. That is not my style. Supreme General, you know full well that the disaster before us is not the rivalry of the states, but the foreign tribes. So why do you stand by and watch the people of Qin and Zhao slaughter one another? Only when the realm is unified and the hearts of the people are brought together can the threat of the foreign tribes truly be resolved. And only Great Qin can pacify the states, so that our people of Yan and Huang will no longer suffer war and may enjoy peace.” Li Mu’s voice carried a trace of anger as he replied, “So you came alone to persuade me to surrender? Never. I, Li Mu, have received the favor of Zhao and bear the duty of easing my ruler’s worries and sharing his burdens. I am a minister of Zhao. If I surrendered, how would the people of the world look at me?” Li Mu drew his sword and pointed it straight at Zhao Ji. Then he continued, “Because you saved the people of my northern border, I will spare your life. Leave at once. Even if you could kill me here by yourself, you still could not escape the encirclement of my army. Besides, even if you did kill me, as long as the Zhao army does not open the gates of Dai, violent Qin will gain nothing from its siege.” After hearing this, Zhao Ji laughed loudly. Even Blood Tiger beside him was roused awake by the noise. As Zhao Ji stroked Blood Tiger’s head to calm it, he said, “Supreme General, you keep saying you are a minister of Zhao. Then may I ask you—where is Zhao’s general now? Where is the State of Zhao? Of Zhao’s vast territory, only Dai remains. The King of Zhao has already been killed by me, and the royal clan and nobles who could have succeeded him have already been escorted by me to Handan. They are no different from sheep waiting to be slaughtered. Zhao is already finished.” Zhao Ji’s words shook Li Mu to his core, and shock spread across his face. Zhao Ji stood and continued, “You no longer have a state to rely on, nor a ruler to serve. And now, for the sake of your personal reputation, you would have the descendants of Yan and Huang slaughter one another? Moreover, the unification of the realm is the will of Heaven. Do you mean to go against Heaven’s will? Tell me—after a thousand years, will you be praised or condemned?” Zhao Ji fixed Li Mu with a steady gaze, his face stern as he spoke. “If I had not come just now, the Zhao people you speak of would already have died at the hands of the nomads. Yet you failed to send aid because your priority was obstructing your own people.” Zhao Ji mounted Blood Tiger and rode away. Turning back, he said to Li Mu, who still stood rooted in place, “Think carefully on my words today, Supreme General. The next time we meet, I hope you will have an answer for me.” Blood Tiger leapt powerfully across several large rocks and was soon gone from sight. General Li Mu remained standing there like a statue, his face full of thought, his eyes darkened, both fists clenched tightly. Zhao Ji and the fierce tiger returned to the Great Qin camp. The moment Zhao Ji came into view, the soldiers immediately reported to General Tu Sui, “Supreme General has returned.” Tu Sui quickly came over and asked, “My lord, you have labored all day. Did you meet Li Mu?” “And what was the result?” Zhao Ji answered confidently, “Nine-tenths success.” Then Zhao Ji led the army forward and said, “Let’s go. We’ll join up with Wang Jian and Huan Yi. Dai will soon be ours.” Zhao Ji led his troops to Wang Jian and Huan Yi. At this time, a wine feast was being held in the military camp. Wang Jian and Huan Yi each held a cup of wine as they came forward, both competing to toast Zhao Ji. Wang Jian said, “Zhao Ji, I, Wang Jian, drink to you. Now that we’ve met today, you must drink this first cup with me.” Huan Yi immediately cut in. “How can that do? It has been hard enough for me to meet an old acquaintance. Zhao Ji should drink this cup with me first.” The two immediately began to argue. Wang Jian raised his voice. “I was the one who wrote to invite Zhao Ji here, so naturally he should drink my cup first.” Zhao Ji looked a little helpless. “You two Supreme Generals, please don’t argue.” Then Zhao Ji raised his cup and said to them both, “I am of the younger generation. It is only proper that I should offer a toast to the two Supreme Generals. Besides, I am a subject of Great Qin. Fighting for Great Qin is only my duty. How would I dare trouble the two of you to toast me first?” The three of them drained their cups together. Huan Yi praised him. “Good, good. A young man who is humble and refined. Zhao Ji, I truly like you more and more.” Wang Jian also chimed in with praise. “When men appreciate each other, what need is there for so many words? So long as one’s heart is full of passion and spirit, that is enough.” As soon as he finished his drink, Wang Jian said, “Zhao Ji, this time, for us to call you all the way here from Handan was truly out of necessity. The two of us really had no other options. Ever since you joined the army, you have always had clever strategies for defeating the enemy, and that is why we invited you here.” Zhao Ji set his cup down on the table and smiled. “This junior understands the difficulties faced by the two Supreme Generals. At present, whether we attack, assault the city, or continue the siege, none of those are good options. So on my way here, I came up with a psychological tactic.” Huan Yi and Wang Jian both looked startled. “A psychological tactic?” Zhao Ji explained his plan. “The Zhao army is certain we would not move rashly, so they have no fear. In that case, let us put on the appearance of a desperate all-out battle and make them afraid. Only when they are afraid will their true nature show. We will force Li Mu to surrender.” Zhao Ji’s face was full of confidence. The plan was quickly set into motion. Following Zhao Ji’s instructions, Wang Jian and Huan Yi led the mighty Great Qin army in an imposing advance to the gates of Dai. The soldiers of Great Qin were full of momentum, with siege weapons prepared and ready to break the city. Wang Jian shouted loudly, “Battering rams, trebuchets, prepare! Today we will bathe Dai in blood!” Huan Yi beside him also roared, “If we do not succeed, then we die trying! This is the kind of bloody battle Great Qin’s men should have fought long ago. What is there to fear?” The Qin soldiers immediately drew their bows and aimed straight at the city of Dai. Tens of thousands of cavalry and infantry shouted in unison, gripping their spears as they charged toward the city gates. Supreme General Li Mu and the court officials standing atop Dai’s walls looked down at the forces of Great Qin in panic. “What do we do now? Wang Jian and Huan Yi’s armies are using all their strength. They really mean to attack with everything they have.” Someone beside them said in alarm, “At first I thought they would never waste troops over a tiny city like Dai. Why would they suddenly do this?” Li Mu said nothing, only gazing downward in deep thought. Around him, voices rose in anxious discussion. “I heard that Zhao Ji of violent Qin was summoned to Dai yesterday. This attack must certainly be his idea.” “That god of slaughter? I heard he is bloodthirsty and loves battle. It seems this siege is no act.” Another official panicked and turned to run. “Go quickly! If those men risk their lives to hold them off, the city won’t fall immediately. It should be enough time for us to flee into Yan.” Li Mu’s face instantly darkened with rage. Turning around, he slapped those officials across the face. “What do you people mean by this? We are the soldiers of Dai and carry the blood of Zhao within us. We are not straw and weeds to be thrown away.” One of the officials pointed at Li Mu’s face and said, “You lowborn thing, you were only ever a shield against the foreign tribes, yet you dare call yourself a man of Zhao?” Another beside him folded his arms and sneered, “We only honored you as Supreme General because you had a few troops under your command. Don’t think yourself so capable that you can shout at us. Are you worthy?” At that moment, Zhao Ji’s earlier words echoed through Li Mu’s mind: “Supreme General, our shared roots as one people are threatened by foreign tribes. We are all descendants of Yan and Huang—why must we slaughter one another?” Li Mu suddenly realized that Zhao Ji, a man of Qin, at least knew they shared a common hatred, while these people before him were truly detestable. Li Mu said to those hateful Zhao ministers, "All you want is to use the flesh and blood of my men of Dai to protect your own lives." One of the ministers behind him glanced over and replied, "Ridiculous. There has always been high and low in this world. Otherwise, wouldn't all ritual and order fall into chaos?" The man beside him immediately cut in, "Why waste words on a vulgar boor like him? It only lowers our own status. Let's go." Suddenly, from behind Li Mu, an arrow carrying a wine gourd shot over, startling him. The arrow bearing the gourd slammed hard into the wall. Its impact was terrifying, and the struck section of wall shattered, fragments flying everywhere. The two ministers screamed in fright, "Heavens! Tyrant Qin! Tyrant Qin is attacking!" Riding the Blood Tiger with bow in hand, Zhao Ji shouted, "General Li, I truly do not wish to see the descendants of Yan and Huang slaughter one another, but I have no choice, for the great cause of unifying the realm still remains. I know you understand righteousness, so now I ask you this: do you truly wish to watch Zhao and Qin destroy each other, only for other tribes to reap the benefits?" Pointing at the Qin soldiers, Zhao Ji continued, "Look carefully at these six hundred thousand young soldiers, filled with passion. They clearly could have joined forces with you, fought with one heart against foreign enemies, and protected Huaxia together. Yet now they are being driven to the point of slaughtering their own kind." Zhao Ji rode up close to the city gate and looked up at Li Mu. "If, General, you truly understand this greater cause, then I am willing to stop the war and withdraw. Great Qin will guarantee the safety of all officers and soldiers within the city, and keep Dai secure. We can sit together, drink the fine wine of Huaxia, and join forces against foreign invaders. But if you are unwilling, then this cup of wine will be my tribute to the soldiers of Qin and Zhao who are about to die beneath my sword." "Like sons of Yan and Huang, we should drink good wine together and fight foreign enemies together." As soon as he finished speaking, Zhao Ji uncapped the wine gourd and drained it in great gulps, showing his resolve. The surrounding soldiers all shouted in unison, "Like sons of Yan and Huang, we should drink good wine together and fight foreign enemies together!" A general at Li Mu's side, his face full of worry and confusion, said, "General, they are ready to die to take the city. Our chances of victory are very slim. Do we really want to fight?" Another added, "We have defended our homeland and fought off many invading states before. But after this battle, I'm afraid those states will all profit from our mutual destruction." Li Mu held the wine gourd in his hand and fell into deep thought. That Zhao minister pointed at Li Mu's face again and shouted, "Defending Zhao against the Qin army is our duty. How can we surrender? Li Mu, send out the troops at once!" Li Mu was enraged by those words. "A moment ago you were calling us lowly commoners, and now you want us to throw away our lives for a Zhao state that has already perished!" Then Li Mu said no more and emptied the gourd in one breath. Li Mu smashed the gourd hard against the city wall. He turned and ordered the soldiers, "Men, seize that pack of incompetents who only wanted to flee to Yan, and tie them all up for me!" Those ministers were instantly terrified, too frightened to keep cursing. One of them cried out, "Do you think Qin will spare you just because you surrender?" "You fool! You are the disgrace of Zhao!" Li Mu's eyes turned icy and his voice dropped. "Wasn't it you who said I was unworthy of being a man of Zhao?" "I simply do not wish for a hundred thousand soldiers and the common people of this land to slaughter one another for a Zhao state that fell long ago." Then Li Mu turned and shouted, "Open the city gates at once and welcome our compatriots into the city!" The soldiers behind him obeyed with one heart. The gates of Dai were opened, and when the Qin soldiers saw this, they erupted in cheers. "Dai has surrendered! We don't have to fight anymore!" What had happened was somewhat unexpected. Even Wang Jian was surprised. "Li Mu surrendered? Is it real or not?" Huan Yi beside him replied, "The city gates are already open. How could it be fake? Zhao Ji, you have saved the lives of many soldiers." Zhao Ji said to Wang Jian and Huan Yi, "Li Mu did not surrender. He merely chose his own people." As the city gates stood open, General Li Mu walked out holding his wine gourd high. A system notification appeared. Conquered Dai. The player's great achievement in destroying Zhao has been completed. Outside Dai, it was already night. Inside the city, a wine banquet was underway. Wang Jian raised his cup to Li Mu and said, "Welcome, General Li Mu, to Great Qin." Then he looked around and asked, "Where did Zhao Ji go? How can this banquet possibly be without him?" Huan Yi replied, "He said he can't hold his drink well and has gone to rest. He's been worn out for days, so don't disturb him." Late at night, Zhao Ji used the excuse of returning to his room to check the system. Zhao Ji opened the system and ordered it, "Settle the mission rewards." A system screen appeared. Player command received. Congratulations, player, on completing the mission. Beast Taming specialty successfully unlocked. Successfully killed the King of Zhao and exterminated Zhao. Does the player wish to receive this Beast Taming skill? Zhao Ji answered happily, "I finally unlocked it. Happily accept." The system screen displayed: Player command received. Activating Beast Taming skill. Beginning skill transmission. Skill transmission complete. The player's current skill is Level 1. At that moment, a small flame appeared in Zhao Ji's hand. Somewhat disappointed, he said, "It doesn't feel like anything changed at all." The system screen displayed Zhao Ji's current stats. Character: Zhao Ji. Secondary specialty: Beginner Beast Taming, Level 1. Can communicate with wild beasts and birds. Beast Taming skill: Taming Aura. Can tame small creatures not exceeding Level 1. Tamed divine beast: bird-beast, Level 12. Innate Second Layer Realm. Physical strength: 3,000. True qi: acquired cultivation technique. Completed basic content of the Heavenly Origin Divine Art, inexhaustible vitality. Can restore true qi and cultivate martial arts. Completed most basic swordsmanship: one strike releases invisible sword qi. Completed intermediate swordsmanship. Ferocious Tiger Fist: each punch carries a tiger's roar effect and can create an explosion with greatly multiplied lethality. Original physical strength completed. Archery skill: Divine Arrow Art, completed. Comprehended Three Hundred Arrows Without Missing, Practical Linked Shots, Tiger-Infused Arrow. Completed comprehension of the Overlord Halberd technique. Owned weapons: Overlord Halberd, Qinggang Sword. Armor, Ten-Stone Bow, Eight Treasures. Owned attribute: winning hearts and minds. Army-training attribute: can command armies and help the player's side maintain one hundred percent morale and combat power. Owned attribute: authority of a supreme general; all subordinate generals stand in awe. Experience needed for next level: 38,650. After reading it, Zhao Ji sighed. "No wonder the level is so low. System, can you raise the Beast Taming skill level a bit more? At this low a level, do you expect me to go tame sparrows?" The system replied, "Skill levels can be upgraded using points. Does the player wish to upgrade now? Raise it to the highest possible level. Beginning point conversion." At once, countless fierce beasts appeared in Zhao Ji's mind: eagles, savage wolves, phoenixes. The system notified him: "Congratulations. Beast Taming has been raised one level to Level 2, one level to Level 3, one level to Level 4. Maximum level reached. The player may now tame any wild beast or bird below Level 11. The player has 600 points remaining." Zhao Ji said, "Now that's more like it. For the time being, this level should be enough for me to use." Zhao Ji took out a piece of blue jade from his robes and looked at it with some melancholy. In the blink of an eye, three years had already passed since he left the village. "Now that Zhao has been destroyed, all I need is an edict from the palace, and then I can go back to see her. Wait for me." The next day, the three generals Wang Jian, Huan Yi, and Li Mu came before Zhao Ji. Wang Jian raised a cup and said, "Come, Zhao Ji, drain this cup with this old man and train your tolerance. When we gather again in Xianyang, we won't leave until we're drunk." Huan Yi spoke up as well, "I, Huan Yi, have never forced anyone before. Who would have thought you'd agree so quickly to return to Handan?" Wang Jian immediately cut in on Zhao Ji's behalf. "Returning to Handan is because he is obeying his superior's orders to take over the position of supreme general and rebuild the great camp. With something this good, why wouldn't he agree?" Then he turned to Zhao Ji and said curiously, "This time, when you return to Handan, you will truly become a mighty supreme general guarding a whole region. We are all happy for you. Once everything is arranged properly, then return to Xianyang. His Majesty will surely reward you generously." Zhao Ji smiled and replied, "Then I'll accept General Wang's kind words." The old general answered at once, "No need to be so polite." "Our relationship is already this close. Just call me Uncle Wang." Huan Yi added, "Call me Uncle Huan too, Zhao Ji. Last time I returned to Xianyang to take office, Li Si was quite harshly opposed to you. If he keeps it up this time, you needn't be courteous with him. Old men like us will be a solid backing for you." Zhao Ji immediately clasped his hands and bowed respectfully. "Many thanks for the favor, Uncle Wang, Uncle Huan. Zhao Ji will remember it." Inwardly he thought, "The Meng family has always looked out for me, and now I also have Wang Jian and Huan Yi by my side. Even if I have to go to court, no one will be able to stand against me anymore." Wang Jian and Huan Yi mounted their horses, then turned back and said to Zhao Ji, "Then set out early. Old Huan and I still have a few matters to finish here. We will surely meet again in Xianyang later." Li Mu said to Wang Jian and Huan Yi, "You two generals may go on ahead. I wish to stay a little longer to see General Zhao off." Watching the two generals ride away, Zhao Ji asked Li Mu, "General Li, is there something else you wish to say to me?" Li Mu knelt before Zhao Ji and said, "General Zhao, please accept this bow from your subordinate." Li Mu's action startled Zhao Ji. "General Li, what do you mean by this?" Li Mu continued, "General Zhao, this time, being able to preserve peace in Dai is enough to satisfy my heart. Yet the King of Qin even granted me grace to continue guarding Dai. I know this is because you spoke a few words for me before the King of Qin." "General Zhao, here and now I swear that my three hundred thousand troops will be integrated into Qin. However, if one day General Zhao gives an order, then even if I must defy the mandate of Heaven, I will still obey your command and serve you with absolute loyalty, even if it means plunging into boiling water or fire." Hearing those words, Zhao Ji realized, "Li Mu has suddenly taken the initiative to submit to me like this. He must have guessed at least part of what I am thinking. But friendship between gentlemen has never needed so many words. For now, I'll just accept his sincerity." Then Zhao Ji replied to Li Mu, "Good. I understand General Li's intentions." Suddenly a loud voice called out, "My lord! My lord!" Zhao Ji, who had been slumped over the table, abruptly woke at Tu Sui's voice. "Tu Sui, did I fall asleep?" Tu Sui stepped forward and replied, "Since returning to Handan, my lord has done nothing but handle official duties. You have not rested for over half a month. It is only natural that you would collapse from exhaustion. I have already integrated all the surrendered soldiers with our own forces, and the Zhao Regional Army has also been established. We now await the general's orders." Hearing this, Zhao Ji held his head, feeling somewhat weary. He thought, "Right. It's already been half a month since I returned from Dai to Handan. Yet in my dreams, I still think I'm in Dai. I've really worked myself half mad." Then Zhao Ji stood and said to Tu Sui, "Well done. Pass down the order to prepare to depart for Xianyang. This time, two thousand personal guards accompanying me will be enough." Tu Sui said worriedly, "My lord, do you not need rest? Recover for a few more days. You are truly too exhausted." Zhao Ji replied, "No need." The next day, the force preparing to return to Xianyang assembled. At the command to depart, the Supreme General set out. Zhao Ji sat in the carriage, lifting the curtain to look outside. "If I meet the King of Qin one day sooner, I can rest one day sooner and prepare to return home one day sooner. After being away from Li Village for all these years, I finally understand what it means to long to go home." Ten days later, Zhao Ji's party arrived at Mount Xia in the outskirts of Xianyang. Not far away, Qin Sheng had long been standing there in command of a unit of Imperial Guards. Seeing this, Wei Cai spurred his horse up beside the carriage and anxiously reported to Zhao Ji, "Supreme General, Xianyang lies just ahead, but Qin Sheng is there below the city with the Imperial Guards. I do not know what this means." Zhao Ji lifted the curtain and looked ahead, then said, "Don't be tense yet. Move forward and take a look first." Wei Cai nodded and obeyed. "Understood." Zhao Ji's party continued onward. Though he said that, Zhao Ji, sitting in the carriage, could not help feeling uneasy. "The Imperial Guards are blocking us outside the city. This must be one of Ying Zheng's arrangements. What is he planning? Could it be that Ying Zheng listened to Li Si's slander and is now guarding against me? Is he afraid my great merits will lead me to usurp the throne? If so, I need to make preparations early. But I still feel that Ying Zheng shouldn't be that kind of person." After advancing for a while, Zhao Ji's party finally came face to face with Qin Sheng's force. At that moment, Zhao Ji slowly lifted the carriage curtain, and said in a sharp voice, "The one blocking the way ahead is General Qin Sheng, is it not? What is the meaning of the Imperial Guards being here?" Hearing this, Qin Sheng quickly dismounted, dropped to one knee, and said excitedly, "Supreme General, there is no need for you to alight from the carriage." Then Qin Sheng began explaining why he was there. "Supreme General, from the moment you entered Xianyang territory, His Majesty led the court officials and the people of the city to wait in welcome. This subordinate was ordered by His Majesty to come and receive Supreme General Zhao Ji in triumph as he returns to the capital. I ask the Supreme General to remain steadily seated in your carriage and follow me quickly into the city." Hearing this explanation, Zhao Ji realized he had misunderstood and gave an awkward smile. His tone softened as well. "Then I'll trouble the general to lead the way." Inwardly, Zhao Ji could not help reproaching himself. "In the end, it was my own petty heart. Ying Zheng, as King of Qin, personally led the officials out to welcome me and gave me such grand honor." Then Zhao Ji's party resumed their journey toward the capital. At that moment, Zhao Ji thought again, "Ying Zheng, if you truly treat me like this, then I, Zhao Ji, will certainly never betray you. And if your sons can also remain this sincere, then I too can help you protect Great Qin's realm and keep the land of Yan and Huang unified." Meanwhile, at the city gate, the King of Qin had long been waiting there, his solemn face fixed on the road ahead. The ministers behind him saw Zhao Ji's party approaching and cried out in surprise, "Look! Zhao Ji's carriage has arrived!" Qin Sheng led the convoy over. Seeing the King of Qin outside the city, he hurriedly knelt and reported, "Reporting to Your Majesty, your servant Qin Sheng obeyed your order to welcome Supreme General Zhao Ji. The Supreme General has now arrived." Seeing that Zhao Ji had arrived, the King of Qin rushed forward. The ministers behind him panicked and ran after him, trying to stop him. "Your Majesty, please don't go!" Wei Cai, seeing the King come before the convoy and not knowing what was happening, promptly knelt and saluted respectfully. "Y-Your Majesty, this subordinate pays respects to Your Majesty." The King of Qin nodded and said, "Rise," while looking toward the man inside the carriage. He could not help feeling stirred. "Zhao Ji, you and I have finally met." The King of Qin quickly walked to the side of the carriage and lifted the curtain. At that same moment, Zhao Ji also lifted the curtain from inside and came out. The King of Qin and Zhao Ji looked into each other's eyes, both stunned when they saw the other. Zhao Ji thought, "So this is Qin Shi Huang? He actually came to my carriage himself just to lift the curtain for me?" Only then did Zhao Ji recover himself, exclaiming in shock, "Your Majesty!" He immediately dropped to his knees in salute. "Your servant Zhao Ji pays respects to Your Majesty. What merit or virtue do I possess to trouble Your Majesty to step forward in person? I have already settled all matters in Zhao territory and established the great camp at Handan. The whole army numbers three hundred thousand. I have now returned in obedience to Your Majesty's command." The King of Qin hastily stepped forward to help Zhao Ji up, speaking in a warm and gentle tone. "Good, good, good. Rise, Zhao Qing, and speak." As soon as Zhao Ji stood, the King of Qin warmly took Zhao Ji's hand and led him forward, laughing excitedly. "All of you, come and look. This man is Zhao Ji, the number one meritorious official of Great Qin, who has repeatedly rendered extraordinary service over these past three years. For Heaven to bestow Zhao Ji upon Great Qin is the fortune of Great Qin, the fortune of the people, and the happiness of the realm." All the ministers bowed respectfully and called out congratulations to the King. The King of Qin led Zhao Ji to his own royal carriage and said kindly, "Come, Zhao Qing, ride with me. I want everyone to see the bearing of Great Qin's valiant general." Zhao Ji still had not fully recovered from the King's words and stammered, "This servant thanks Your Majesty." Then, still dazed, Zhao Ji was pulled by the King of Qin into the carriage to sit beside him. The King of Qin's carriage and Zhao Ji's procession moved through the streets of the capital, and the people on both sides shouted excitedly, "General Zhao Ji! Supreme General Zhao Ji! Ten thousand years to the King! Supreme General Zhao Ji! Ten thousand years to the King!" At that moment, the King of Qin paid no attention to those cheers. Instead, he stared fixedly at Zhao Ji's face. A thought arose in the King of Qin's mind. "Was I overthinking it before? Yet how can there be someone in this world who looks so much alike? He is the image of Dong'er. If Dong'er and I had a child, he would look just like this, wouldn't he?" But the King of Qin quickly rejected the thought. It was not only the appearance; he had also never felt such intimacy from anyone as he felt from Zhao Ji. Seeing the King of Qin staring at him, Zhao Ji felt his whole body stiffen. "Your Majesty...?" The King of Qin smiled brightly and replied, "It is my gaze that is improper. For many years, I have hoped to meet you. Today that wish has finally been fulfilled." "I am truly delighted." The King of Qin even quickly draped an arm over Zhao Ji's shoulder and said with a broad smile, "Zhao Ji, I am truly satisfied with you." Zhao Ji, having an arm thrown over his shoulder, was still stunned and unable to adjust. The ministers below were just as shocked. Someone said, "Did you see that? His Majesty is actually so close with Zhao Ji?" The ministers beside him immediately explained that Zhao Ji had rendered great service, so of course the King was pleased. The assembled officials then began discussing it animatedly among themselves: the King truly valued Zhao Ji, who had become a Supreme General at such a young age and clearly had boundless prospects ahead of him. A minister standing beside Li Si sighed and said, "Such royal favor is truly one of a kind. From now on, I doubt anyone at court will dare offend this great meritorious official again. Don't you agree, Lord Commandant?" Li Si said nothing outwardly, but inwardly he was already furious. He thought to himself, "Who could have imagined Zhao Ji would rise to his current position? He should have been my son-in-law, but now I must think of a way to win him over again." Inside Zhangtai Palace, the King of Qin took Zhao Ji by the hand and led him inside. This is a little different from what I imagined. Or rather, Ying Zheng is being a bit too intimate with me. Please accept Zhao Ji's bow." General Meng Wu replied cheerfully, "Why are you being so polite? I am Yan'er's adoptive father. Taking care of my daughter is only natural." Xia Wuqie also added, "Ji'er and Xi'er call me Great-Grandpa. This old man has long treated them as my own great-grandchildren." Meng Tian also came up quickly, slung an arm around Zhao Ji, and greeted him with a grin. "Long time no see. Why are you being so formal, brat? Tonight, we don't go home until we're drunk. - Are you creative or analytical? Find out in 5 seconds.: Kind: captions Language: en I would like you to clasp your hands together and keep them in that position for a moment. Some researchers see the brain as having two general modes. In one mode (often called 'right-brained'), it is more intuitive, visual, and creative. In the other (often called 'left-brained'), it is more logical, sequential, and analytical. All of us work in both modes, but naturally tend towards one or the other. According to the theory, if your right thumb is on top of your left thumb then you tend to be a so-called left-brainer, and so are more likely to be verbal and analytical. If your left thumb is on top of your right thumb then you tend to be a so-called right-brainer, and more likely to excel in visual, creative, and intuitive tasks. So, if you want to gain a fun insight into someone, maybe you should ask them to put their hands together.

- Dan Pink: The puzzling secret to motivation (Key Points Talk): Kind: captions Language: en I wanna make a case for rethinking how we run our businesses. Take a look at this. This is called the candle problem and here's how it works. I bring you into a room, I give you a candle, some thumbtacks, and some matches and I say to you: Your job is to attach the candle to the wall so the wax doesn't drip on the table. And eventually after 5 or 10 minutes, most people figure out the solution which you can see here. The key is to overcome what is called functional fixedness. You look at that box and you see it only as a receptacle for the tacks, but it can also have this other function as a platform for the candle. Now, I wanna tell you about an experiment using the candle problem, done by a scientist named Sam Glucksberg - he gathered his participants and he says I'm gonna time you, how quickly you can solve this problem. He offered rewards, he said if you're in the top 25% of the fastest times, you get 5 dollars. If you're the fastest of everyone we're testing here today, you get 20 dollars. How much faster did this group solve the problem? Answer: It took them on average 3 and a half minutes... longer. Three and a half minutes longer, now this makes no sense, right? If you want people to perform better, you reward them, right? Bonuses, commissions, their own reality show, incentivize them. You've got an incentive designed to sharpen thinking and accelerate creativity and it does just the opposite. These contingent motivators: If you do this then you get that work in some circumstances but for a lot of tasks, they actually either don't work or often they do harm. Think about your own work: Are the problems that you face or even the problems we've been talking about here, are those kinds of problems - do they have a clear set of rules and a single solution? No! Those if - then rewards DON'T WORK! Economists at LSE looked at 51 studies of pay for performance plans inside of companies. Here's what the economists there said: "We find that financial incentives can result in a negative impact on overall performance." There's a mismatch between what science knows and what business does. Here's what science knows: 1. Those 20th century rewards, those motivators we think are the natural part of business do work but only in a surprisingly narrow band of circumstances. 2. Those if then rewards often destroy creativity. 3. The secret to high performance isn't rewards and punishments but that unseen intrinsic drive, the drive to do things for their own sake, the drive to do things because they matter. I rest my case.

- How To Understand LinkedIn's Content Distribution Algorithm? - Social Media Business Playbook: Kind: captions Language: en How to understand Linkin's content distribution algorithm. Have you ever wondered how Linkin decides what content appears in your feed? Understanding Linkin's content distribution algorithm can help you create posts that reach a wider audience. Let's break it down in simple terms. When you share a post on LinkedIn, the algorithm starts by checking its quality. It looks for spammy content or anything that doesn't meet community standards. If your post is flagged as lowquality, it won't be shown much at all. However, if it passes this initial check, it gets a chance to shine. Your post is then shown to a small group of your connections. This is like a test run to see how people react. If your post gets a lot of likes, comments, or shares, it signals to the algorithm that your content is engaging. This can lead to wider distribution, allowing it to reach even more people, including those who are not directly connected to you. Several key factors influence how the algorithm determines what content is relevant. First, connection strength plays a big role. If you interact frequently with certain users, their posts will likely appear more often in your feed. The algorithm values meaningful interactions over just having a lot of connections. Next, content relevance is crucial. The algorithm looks at keywords and topics that relate to your interests and past interactions. This helps it match content that you will find meaningful. Engagement metrics are also important. Posts that spark conversations or are shared widely get a boost. This indicates that the content is resonating with users. Consistency matters too. Regularly posting signals to the algorithm that you are an active user. This can help increase the reach of your content over time. The composition of your post matters as well. Using the right number of hashtags, ideally three to five, can help your content get noticed. Avoiding spammy behavior like irrelevant tagging, is essential. It's also wise to space out your posts, allowing at least 12 hours between them. The distribution process happens in stages. First, there is quality filtering where the algorithm checks your post against community standards. Then comes engagement testing where it gauges reactions from a small audience. After that, the algorithm ranks your content based on your network and relevance. Finally, if your post performs well, it gets wider distribution. For businesses using Linkin's publishing platform, understanding this algorithm is vital. Focus on creating highquality, relevant content that speaks to your target audience. Engage consistently and inform meaningful interactions. Have you ever wondered how Google seems to understand your search queries so well? The introduction of the BERT algorithm update is a big part of that story. BERT stands for birectional encoder representations from transformers. This update was rolled out to help Google better understand natural language in search queries. Before BERT, Google often looked at words in isolation or in a limited context. This approach sometimes led to results that miss the mark, especially for longer, more conversational searches. With BERT, Google can analyze words in relation to all other words in a sentence, both before and after a specific word. This means it can grasp the context and nuances of language much more effectively. For example, consider the difference between the phrases, I went to the bank to fish, and I went to the bank to deposit money. The meaning of bank changes based on the surrounding words. BERT helps Google understand these kinds of distinctions, which is essential for delivering accurate search results. This update is particularly beneficial for complex queries where context is key. It allows Google to interpret user intent more like a human would rather than relying solely on keyword matching. This shift is important for marketers and those involved in search engine optimization. With BERT, the focus moves away from keyword stuffing and towards creating content that naturally addresses user intent. Marketers should aim to produce clear context content that answers specific questions. This approach aligns with how people naturally speak or search, making it easier for users to find what they need. In practical terms, this means that if you want your content to rank well, you should prioritize quality over quantity. Think about the questions your audience is asking and provide thorough answers. By doing this, you can improve your visibility in search results and engage more meaningfully with your audience. In essence, Google introduced BERT to enhance its ability to understand language context and user intent. This update has significant implications for how marketers approach content creation in the digital acquisition landscape. By adapting to these changes, you can better connect with your audience and improve your search engine optimization efforts.

I appreciate that it connects books, social media, advertising, and narrative structures into a unified idea of media as a social-shaper.

Still, I believe the piece could push its critique further in several areas. One limitation is its broad brush—it treats “the media” as a singular entity rather than a fragmented, contested space. For instance, different media institutions have vastly different ownership, political ties, and audience profile. Recognizing that heterogeneity would help refine the critique. Also, while the video touches on the idea that media builds “dreams,” it could engage more deeply with resistance—how people interpret, filter, or subvert media messages rather than passively absorb them.

Another dimension I’d like to see more of is empirical: how do these media-constructed identities play out in specific cultural contexts (for example Armenia, the Caucasus, etc.) where media ecosystems differ, local languages matter, and Western models don’t fully apply?

Overall, this video is compelling in its framing of media as more than a mirror—it’s a mold. It invites us to ask: if our world is partly built by stories, who is writing those stories—and who gets to live inside them?
